en: The Perfection of Wisdom in Twenty-five Thousand Lines:

Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha on the Vulture Peak Mountain together with a great saṅgha of monks, about five thousand monks in number, all of whom were arhats whose outflows were exhausted.

Together with approximately five hundred bhikṣuṇīs who were free from afflictions, had attained mastery, whose minds were well-liberated and whose wisdom was well-liberated; who were noble steeds and great elephants, having accomplished their task and fulfilled their duty; who had laid down the burden, achieved their own goal, and exhausted the fetters of existence; whose minds were well-liberated through right knowledge, and who had reached the supreme perfection of mastery over all mental states; as well as with laymen and laywomen.
And together with all those who had seen the Dharma, and with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas—

all of whom had attained the *dhāraṇīs*, dwelt in emptiness, had the signless as their sphere of activity, were unconditioned by vows, had attained the equality of patience, had attained the unattached *dhāraṇīs*, possessed infallible supernormal knowledges, and whose words were authoritative.

They were free from hypocrisy and frivolity; their minds were devoid of seeking reputation or gain; they taught the Dharma without worldly motives; they had reached the further shore of patience regarding the profound Dharma;

they possessed self-confidence; they had transcended the deeds of Māra; their karmic obstructions were stilled; they were skilled in the analytical discernment and exposition of the Dharma; they had well undertaken their vows for incalculable eons; they had smiling faces; they were the first to speak; and their countenances were free from frowns.
They were skilled in singing and conversing through verses; their minds were free from dejection; they possessed an uninterrupted eloquence and the fearlessness of overwhelming infinite assemblies;

they were skilled in the means of escape throughout infinite millions of eons; they had resolved upon the Dharma as being like an illusion, a mirage, the moon reflected in water, a dream, an echo, an optical illusion, a reflection, and a magical creation;

they were skilled in entering the subtle and various inclinations of beings according to their movements within the realms of existence; their minds were unimpeded, and they were endowed with supreme patience.
They were skilled in leading others into the realization of reality as it is; they were sustained by the undertaking of vows for the infinite arrays of all buddha-fields;
they remained constantly and perpetually in meditative absorption through the recollection of the Buddhas of incalculable world-systems; they were skillful in supplicating immeasurable Buddhas;
they were skillful in pacifying various views, latent tendencies, outbursts, and afflictions; and they were skillful in manifesting hundreds of thousands of playful displays of samādhi.
Namely: the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhadrapāla; Ratnākara; Sārthavāha; Naradatta; Varuṇadatta; Śubhagupta; Indradatta; Uttaramati; Viśeṣamati; Vardhamānamati; and Amoghadarśin.
and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Susaṃprasthita, Suvikrāntavikrāmin, Nityodyukta, Anikṣiptadhūra,
Sūryagarbha, Anupamacintin, Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, Mañjuśrī, Vajramati, Ratnamudrāhasta, Nityotkṣiptahasta, and Maitreya;
Thus, together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas led by these foremost ones,

the Blessed One himself prepared a lion throne and sat down. Having assumed the cross-legged posture, set his body straight, and established mindfulness before him, he entered the meditative absorption called the King of Samādhis.
In which all meditative absorptions enter, are included, and converge.
Then the Blessed One, mindful and clearly comprehending, arose from that absorption and, having surveyed all the world-systems with his divine eye, smiled from his entire body.
From beneath him, from the two thousand-spoked wheels on the soles of his feet, there issued forth sixty times sixty hundred-thousand million-billion rays of light.
From the ten toes of his feet, sixty-six hundred thousand *niyutas* of millions of light rays issued forth;
likewise, sixty-six [hundred thousand] from each of his two ankles, sixty-six from each of his two calves, sixty-six from each of his two knee-caps;
likewise, from both thighs, from the waist and navel regions, from both sides, and from the heart and the *śrīvatsa*, the mark of a Great Man.
In this way, from each of the ten fingers of the hands there are sixty-six [rays]; from the two arms, sixty-six;

from the two shoulders, sixty-six; likewise, from the forty teeth of the neck, from the two nostrils, from the two ears, from the two eyes, from the *ūrṇā* in the middle, and from the *uṣṇīṣa* above, there are sixty-six hundred thousand *koṭī-niyuta* of rays.

They issued forth. By those rays, this great trichiliocosm was illuminated and completely suffused; likewise, world-systems in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were suffused and illuminated by that great radiance of rays, and so too in the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, and southwestern directions.
In the northwestern direction, below and above, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā were pervaded and illuminated by that great radiance of light;
and those beings who were pervaded and illuminated by that great radiance of light all became destined for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Then indeed, the Blessed One again smiled from all his pores;
and from each single pore there issued forth sixty hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of rays of light,
by which this great trichiliocosm was illuminated and pervaded.
And by those [rays], world-systems in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated by the light and pervaded;

likewise, in the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, downward, and upward directions, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated by the light and pervaded.
And by that radiance of light, all those beings who were touched became destined for unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
Then, indeed, the Blessed One once again caused the great trichiliocosm world-system to be illuminated by that natural radiance of the Blessed Buddhas;
even so that in each of the ten directions, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated by that radiance.
And those beings who were touched by that light all became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One extended his tongue-faculty, with which he covered this great trichiliocosm world-system.
Having pervaded the trichiliocosm with his tongue-faculty, he smiled from that tongue-faculty,
from which there issued forth many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of rays of light; and upon each tip of every ray, there appeared supreme, golden-hued lotuses with a thousand petals.
And within those lotuses, forms of the Buddha were seated and remained, teaching the Dharma—namely, this very teaching of the Dharma connected with the six perfections.
Having gone to world-systems in the eastern direction beyond as many as the sands of the river Ganges, incalculable and immeasurable, they taught the Dharma to sentient beings;
likewise in the south, the west, the north, below, above, and in the intermediate directions.

And in each of the ten directions, having gone to immeasurable world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, they taught the Dharma to sentient beings; that is to say, this very teaching of the Dharma connected with the six perfections.
And those sentient beings who heard that teaching of the Dharma became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

Then, indeed, the Blessed One, seated upon that very lion-throne, entered the meditative absorption called "The Lion’s Play" (siṃhavikrīḍita). He performed such a miraculous feat (ṛddhyabhisaṃskāra) that, by means of this performed miraculous feat, this great trichiliocosm shook, trembled, and quaked in six ways.
It shook, it moved forward, it trembled violently; it quivered, it quivered forward, it quivered violently; it resounded, it resounded forward, it resounded violently.
It shook, it shook violently, it shook intensely;
it roared, it roared loudly, it roared intensely;
at its edges it rose up while in the middle it sank down.
It rose in the center and sank at the edges;
it was soft and smooth, producing happiness for all sentient beings.
Then, in that very instant, moment, and second, all the hells, animal realms, and worlds of Yama within this great trichiliocosm were completely cut off and became empty.
All unfavorable conditions came to an end;
and those beings who had passed away from those states of hell, the animal realm, and the world of Yama were all, through that very joy and gladness, reborn into the common lot of human beings,
and likewise reborn into the common lot of the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Thirty-three, the Yāma, the Tuṣita, the Nirmāṇarati, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin.
Then indeed, those humans and those gods, through the very power of the Blessed One, recollected their former births;
and having recollected them, with that same joy and gladness, they approached the place where the Blessed One was.
Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and, with palms joined, paid homage to the Blessed One.

In this way, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the eastern direction— and likewise in the southern, western, and northern directions, in the intermediate directions, above, below, and all around throughout the ten directions— in each and every directional sector, within world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā,
all hells, all animal births, and all realms of Yama were completely cut off and became empty.
All unfavorable conditions came to an end;
and those beings who had passed away from those states of hell, the animal realm, and the world of Yama were all reborn among gods and humans,
and having been reborn among gods and humans, through the very power of the Blessed One, they [recalled] their former births.

They recollected [their past vows], and having recollected them, with that very same joy and gladness, they approached the presence of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who had arisen in their respective Buddha-fields;
having approached and prostrated at the feet of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, they all stood with palms joined in reverence and paid homage to the Blessed One.
Then, indeed, those beings in this trichiliocosm who were blind from birth saw forms with their eyes;
those beings who were deaf heard sounds with their ears;
and those who were insane regained their mindfulness.
Those with distracted minds became single-minded; those who were hungry had their bodies satisfied;
and those who were thirsty were freed from thirst.
Those touched by disease became free from disease; those with impaired faculties had their faculties restored to fullness;
and those who were not separated from unwholesome conduct of body, speech, and mind, and livelihood, became separated from unwholesome conduct of body, speech, and mind, and livelihood.

All sentient beings came to possess minds equal toward their mothers and fathers, minds equal toward their brothers and sisters, and minds equal toward their friends, ministers, kinsmen, and blood relations; they became practitioners of the ten paths of wholesome action.
They were celibate, pure, and possessed the fragrance of freedom from illness; all sentient beings were endowed with every happiness—such was their happiness.

They attained it, just like a monk who has entered the third dhyāna; and at that very moment, they became endowed with such wisdom that the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, residing in other buddha-fields, uttered this exclamation: "Excellent is self-control! Excellent is tranquility! Excellent is restraint! Excellent is the practice of the holy life! Excellent!"
Then, indeed, the Blessed One, seated upon that very lion-throne,
remained surpassing this triple-thousand great-thousand world-system, shining, glowing, heating, and radiating with splendor, color, glory, and brilliance.

In the eastern direction, in the southern, western, and northern directions, below, above, and in the intermediate directions, the Tathāgata remains, having surpassed world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges,
shining, glowing, heating, and radiating with light,
color, splendor, and brilliance.
Just as Sumeru, the king of mountains, stands surpassing all other mountains, shining, glowing, blazing, and radiating with its splendor, color, majesty, and brilliance,
even so the Blessed One stands surpassing all world-systems, shining, glowing, blazing, and radiating.
He was endowed with a complexion, splendor, and majesty that were free from fear.
Then, indeed, the Blessed One once again manifested an ordinary physical body equal to the bodies of the beings within this triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system.
At that time, those gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm and the Śubhakṛtsna realm who were in this triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system...
The Ābhāsvara gods, the Brahmakāyika gods, the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods,

the Tuṣita gods, the Yāma gods, the Trāyastriṃśa gods, and the Cāturmahārājakāyika gods— having seen that unsatisfiable physical form of the Tathāgata, [offered] divine flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards.

Having taken divine blue lotuses, white lotuses, fragrant lotuses, red lotuses, and pink lotuses, and having taken divine saffron and tamāla leaves, they approached the Tathāgata’s enchanting physical form;
and those humans who were here in this trichiliocosm mahāsāhasra world system also [approached] that enchanting [form] of the Tathāgata.
Having beheld the Tathāgata’s peerless physical form, they took flowers grown on land and in water and approached the place where the Tathāgata’s enchanting body was located.

Then those gods and humans scattered that body of the Tathāgata with those divine flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards, as well as with those flowers grown on land and in water.

They showered [the Blessed One]. Then, indeed, all those showers of flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory banners— both those born on land and those born in water— with which the Blessed One was strewn, remained suspended in the air above the Blessed One.
By his miraculous power, a single gabled pavilion appeared, equal in size to a trichiliocosm great thousandfold world system.
From that gabled pavilion hung and dangled those divine flower garlands and silk streamers;
and by means of those flower and silk garlands, this trichiliocosm great thousandfold world system was exceedingly beautified.
And by that golden-colored radiance of the Blessed One’s power, which spread through the ten directions, world-systems in each direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were illuminated;
and in this great trichiliocosm, in all the world-systems consisting of four continents, it occurred to each one of those gods and humans:
"The Tathāgata is seated before me, teaching the Dharma.
Then the Blessed One, remaining seated upon that very lion-throne, again manifested a smile;
by the radiance of that smile, this great trichiliocosm was completely suffused.
When the world-systems in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, were filled [with light],
all those beings in this trichiliocosm saw the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world-systems in the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges;
and all those beings in the world-systems in that eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, saw this [world].
They beheld the Sahā world-system and the Tathāgata Śākyamuni together with the community of monks. In the same way,

they saw the Buddhas in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the southern direction, in the western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, downward, and upward directions.

They beheld the Blessed One together with his assembly of disciples; and all those beings who were in those world-systems, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, saw this Sahā world-system and the Tathāgata Śākyamuni together with the community of monks.
Then, having passed beyond world-systems in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, from the very last of them—
In that world-system named Ratnāvatī, there dwells, remains, and maintains his life a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Ratnākara;
he teaches this very Dharma of the perfection of wisdom to the bodhisattvas.
Then, in that world-system, a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Samantaraśmi [beheld] that great radiance.
Having seen that great earthquake and having beheld the Lord’s incomparable physical form,
he approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnākara;
having approached and bowed at the feet of that Blessed One, he addressed the Tathāgata Ratnākara as follows:
"Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition,
for the appearance of this great radiance in the world, for this great earthquake of the earth, and for the manifestation of this Tathāgata’s most wondrous physical form?"
When this had been said, the Tathāgata Ratnākara spoke thus to the bodhisattva Samantaraśmi:

"Noble son, to the west of here, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is a world-system named Sahā. There, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni dwells, remains, and maintains his life."
He reveals the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas; such is his majestic power.
Then the bodhisattva Samantaraśmi said this to the Tathāgata Ratnākara:
"Blessed One, I shall go to that Sahā world-system in order to behold that Tathāgata Śākyamuni."

In order to pay homage and attend upon those bodhisattva mahāsattvas— who for the most part were youthful, had attained the *dhāraṇīs*, were skilled in the production of meditative concentrations, and had reached the perfection of mastery over all meditative concentrations—
the Blessed One said:
"Go, noble son, whenever you deem it the right time.
Then the Tathāgata Ratnākara gave to the Bodhisattva Samantaraśmi lotuses made of various jewels, shining with gold and having a thousand petals, saying:
"Noble son, with these lotuses you should scatter over that Tathāgata Śākyamuni."

And you should say this: "The Blessed One Ratnākara inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, physical lightness, vigor, well-being, strength, and comfortable dwelling.
And these lotuses have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Awakened One Ratnākara, to the Blessed One.
Furthermore, O son of good family, may you be one who acts with full awareness in that buddha-field. For what reason?"
For those bodhisattvas who have been born there in that Sahā world-system are indeed difficult to approach.

Then, the bodhisattva Samantaraśmi, having taken from the presence of the Tathāgata Ratnākara those lotuses made of various jewels— shining with the brilliance of gold and possessing a thousand petals— together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas, departed.

Surrounded and escorted by householders and renunciants, as well as by boys and girls, he proceeded toward the eastern direction, honoring, respecting, revering, and worshiping the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in those world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards.
He arrived at this Sahā world-system and approached the Tathāgata Śākyamuni; having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.
Standing to one side, the bodhisattva Samantaraśmi addressed the Blessed One Śākyamuni as follows:
"The Blessed One Ratnākara inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, physical lightness, well-being, strength, and whether you dwell in comfort;
and these [gifts] have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnākara."

Lotuses made of various jewels, shining like gold and possessing a thousand petals, were sent to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, took those lotuses and cast them toward those world systems in the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā; and by those lotuses, those world systems became completely filled.
And upon those lotuses sat forms of the Buddha,

and in those buddha-fields they taught the Dharma— namely, this very teaching of the Dharma connected with the perfection of wisdom— and those beings by whom that Dharma was heard became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Then indeed, those bodhisattvas, those householders, those renunciants, those boys, and those girls,
having come from that world-system Ratnāvatī together with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Samantaraśmi,
honored, revered, and venerated the Blessed One Śākyamuni by means of their respective roots of merit.
Having paid homage, they sat down to one side.

Then, indeed, having passed beyond world-systems in the southern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is a world-system at the very limit of them called Sarvaśokāpagata; there dwells a Tathāgata, Arhat, named Aśokaśrī.
The Perfectly Enlightened One dwells, remains, and maintains himself;
he teaches this very Perfection of Wisdom as the Dharma for the Bodhisattvas.
Then, in that world-system, there was a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Vigataśoka who [beheld] that great radiance.
Having seen that great earthquake and having beheld the unsurpassed physical form of the Blessed One,
he approached the place where the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Aśokaśrī was;
having approached and bowed at the feet of that Blessed One, he addressed the Tathāgata Aśokaśrī as follows:
"Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition,
for the appearance of this great radiance in the world, for this great earthquake of the earth, and for the manifestation of this Tathāgata’s most wondrous physical form?"
When this had been said, the Tathāgata Aśokaśrī spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Vigataśoka:

"Noble son, in the northern direction, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system named Sahā. There, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni resides, stays, and maintains his life."
He reveals the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) to the bodhisattvas, the great beings; such is his majestic power.
Then the bodhisattva Vigataśoka addressed the Tathāgata Aśokaśrī as follows:
"Blessed One, I shall go to that Sahā world-system in order to behold that Tathāgata Śākyamuni."

In order to pay homage and attend upon them— and upon those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who for the most part were youthful, had attained dhāraṇīs, were skilled in the production of samādhis, and had reached the perfection of mastery over all samādhis—
the Blessed One said:
"Go, son of good family, at whatever time you deem appropriate.
Then the Tathāgata Aśokaśrī gave to the Bodhisattva Vigataśoka lotuses made of various jewels, shining with gold and having a thousand petals, saying:
"With these lotuses, son of good family, you should scatter them over that Tathāgata Śākyamuni."
And you should say this:
"The Blessed One Aśokaśrī inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from affliction, freedom from illness, ease of movement, well-being, strength, and comfortable dwelling;
and these lotuses have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One Aśokaśrī, to the Blessed One."
"And may you, son of good family, be one who acts with clear comprehension in that buddha-field. For what reason?
Because those bodhisattvas who have been born there in this Sahā world-system are difficult to approach.
Then the bodhisattva Vigataśoka [received] from the presence of the Tathāgata Aśokaśrī those [objects] made of various jewels.

Holding lotuses that shone like gold and had a thousand petals, he was surrounded and escorted by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas— both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls— and while honoring and revering the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in those world-systems in the southern direction that were as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.
Honoring and worshipping with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards,
he arrived at this Sahā world-system and approached the place where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni was.
Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he stood to one side.

Standing to one side, the Bodhisattva Vigataśoka addressed the Blessed One Śākyamuni as follows: "The Blessed One Aśokaśrī inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from affliction, freedom from disease, ease of movement, well-being, strength, and whether you dwell in comfort."

And these lotuses, made of various jewels and shining with the brilliance of gold, each having a thousand petals, were sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Aśokaśrī, to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, took those lotuses and cast them toward those world systems in the southern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā.
And those world-systems were filled with those lotuses;
and upon those lotuses sat forms of Buddhas, who were teaching the Dharma in those Buddha-fields— namely, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the perfection of wisdom.
And those beings by whom that Dharma was heard became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Then indeed, those bodhisattvas, those householders, those renunciants, those boys,
and those girls [were brought] from the world-system Sarvaśokāpagatā by the bodhisattva mahāsattva Vigataśoka.

Having arrived together with their respective roots of merit, they honored, revered, respected, and worshiped the Blessed One Śākyamuni, and then sat down to one side. Then, having passed through world systems in the western direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, from those [worlds], there was one situated at the very limit.
In that world-system named Upaśāntā, there dwells, remains, and maintains his life a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Ratnārcis;
he teaches this very Perfection of Wisdom as the Dharma for Bodhisattvas.
Now, in that world-system, there was a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Cāritramati who [beheld] that great radiance.

Having seen that great earthquake and having beheld the Blessed One’s most wondrous physical form, he approached the place where the Blessed One Ratnārcis, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha was; having approached and bowed at the feet of that Blessed One, he addressed the Tathāgata Ratnārcis as follows:
"Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition,
for the appearance in the world of this great radiance, this great earthquake, and the manifestation of the Tathāgata’s most wondrous physical form?"
When this had been said, the Tathāgata Ratnārcis spoke thus to the bodhisattva Cāritramati:

"Noble son, to the east of here, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system named Sahā. There, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni dwells, remains, and sustains himself."
He reveals the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas; such is his majestic power.
Then the bodhisattva Cāritramati said this to the Tathāgata Ratnārcis:
"Blessed One, I shall go to that Sahā world-system and to..."

To see, pay homage to, and attend upon the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, as well as those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who for the most part were youths, had attained dhāraṇīs, were skilled in the production of samādhis, and had reached the perfection of mastery over all samādhis.
That Blessed One said:
"Go, noble son, whenever you deem it the right time.
Then the Tathāgata Ratnārcis gave to the Bodhisattva Cāritramati lotuses made of various jewels, shining with gold and having a thousand petals, saying:
"Noble son, with these lotuses you should scatter over that Tathāgata Śākyamuni."
And you should say this:
"The Blessed One Ratnārcis inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from affliction, freedom from illness, lightness of body, vigor, well-being, strength, and comfortable dwelling;
and these lotuses have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One Ratnārcis, to the Blessed One."
"And may you, noble son, be one who acts with clear comprehension in that buddha-field. Why is that?
Because those bodhisattvas who have been born there in this Sahā world-system are difficult to approach.
Then the bodhisattva Cāritramati, from the presence of the Tathāgata Ratnārcis, [received] those [objects] made of various jewels...

Holding lotuses that shone like gold and possessed a thousand petals, he was surrounded and escorted by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas— both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls— and while honoring and revering the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in those world-systems in the western direction that were as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, he proceeded.
Honoring and worshipping with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards,
he arrived at this Sahā world-system and approached the place where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni was.
Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he stood to one side.
Standing to one side, the bodhisattva Cāritramati said this to the Blessed One Śākyamuni:
"The Blessed One Ratnārcis inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, physical lightness, ease of movement, vigor, strength, and dwelling in comfort."
And these thousand-petaled lotuses, made of various jewels and radiant with gold, were sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnārcis, to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, took those lotuses and cast them toward those world systems in the western direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā.
Those world-systems were filled with those lotuses,
and upon those lotuses sat forms of the Buddha, teaching the Dharma in those buddha-fields— namely, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the perfection of wisdom—
and those beings who heard that true Dharma became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Then indeed, those bodhisattvas, those householders, those renunciants, those boys, and those girls,
having come together with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Cāritramati from that world-system Upaśāntā,
honored, revered, and venerated the Blessed One Śākyamuni with their respective roots of merit.
Having paid homage, they sat down to one side.

Then, indeed, having passed beyond world-systems in the northern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is a world-system that is the very last of them called Jaya; therein dwells, remains, and maintains his life the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Jayendra.
He teaches this very Perfection of Wisdom as the Dharma for the Bodhisattvas.
Then, in that world-system, a Bodhisattva named Jayadatta, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake, and having seen the Lord’s most beautiful physical form, approached the Lord.
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jayendra approached him; having approached, he bowed at the feet of that Blessed One and said this to the Tathāgata Jayendra:
"Blessed One, what is the cause?"
"What is the cause for the appearance of this great radiance in the world, for this great earthquake of the earth, and for the manifestation of the Tathāgata’s wondrously beautiful body?
When this was said, the Tathāgata Jayendra spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Jayadatta:

"Noble son, there is, in the southern direction, beyond worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, a world-system named Sahā. There, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni dwells, remains, and sustains himself;
he thoroughly proclaims the perfection of wisdom to the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, and such is his majestic power."
Then the bodhisattva Jayadatta said this to the Tathāgata Jayendra:
"Blessed One, I shall go to that Sahā world-system in order to see, pay homage to, and attend upon that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who for the most part are still youths."
They had attained the dhāraṇīs, were skilled in the production of meditative concentrations, and had reached the perfection of mastery over all samādhis.
The Blessed One said:
"Go, noble son, whenever you deem it the right time."
Then the Tathāgata Jayendra gave to the Bodhisattva Jayadatta lotuses made of various jewels, shining with gold and having a thousand petals, saying:
"Noble son, with these lotuses you should scatter over that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and speak thus:"
The Blessed One Jayendra inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from affliction, freedom from illness, lightness of body, vigor, well-being, and comfortable dwelling.
Furthermore, these lotuses have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Jayendra, to the Blessed One.
And may you, noble son, be one who acts with full awareness in that buddha-field. For what reason?
For those bodhisattvas who have been reborn there in the Sahā world-system are indeed difficult to approach.

Then, the bodhisattva Jayadatta, having taken from the presence of the Tathāgata Jayendra those lotuses made of various jewels— shining like gold and possessing a thousand petals— together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas, departed.

Surrounded and escorted by householders, renunciants, boys, and girls, he proceeded toward the northern direction, honoring, revering, respecting, and worshipping the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in those world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards.
He arrived at this Sahā world-system and approached the Tathāgata Śākyamuni; having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.
Standing to one side, the Bodhisattva Jayadatta addressed the Blessed One Śākyamuni as follows:
"The Blessed Lord Jayendra inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from affliction, freedom from illness, physical lightness, ease of movement, vitality, strength, and dwelling in comfort.
Furthermore, the Blessed Tathāgata Jayendra has sent these thousand-petaled lotuses, made of various jewels and shining with the luster of gold, to the Blessed One."

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, took those lotuses and cast them toward those world systems in the northern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; by those lotuses, those world systems were completely filled,
and within those lotuses sat forms of Buddhas who taught the Dharma in those Buddha-fields— namely, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the perfection of wisdom.
And those beings by whom that Dharma was heard became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Then indeed, those bodhisattvas, those householders, those renunciants, those boys,
and those girls came from that world-system Jayā together with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Jayadatta.
Having honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the Blessed One Śākyamuni with their respective roots of merit, they sat down to one side.

Then, having passed beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the northeastern direction, there is a world-system that is the very last of them, named Samādhyalaṅkṛtā; in that [world-system] dwells a Tathāgata named Samādhihastyuttaraśrī.
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, currently resides, stays, and maintains himself;
he teaches this very Perfection of Wisdom as the Dharma for Bodhisattvas.
Now, in that world-system, there was a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Vijayavikrāmin who [beheld] that great radiance.
Having seen that great earthquake and having beheld the Lord’s most wondrous physical form,
he approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Samādhihastyuttaraśrī.
Having approached and bowed at the feet of that Blessed One, he addressed the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Samādhihastyuttaraśrī, as follows:
"O Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition,
for the appearance in the world of this great radiance, of this great earthquake, and of the manifestation of this most wonderful body of a Tathāgata?"
When this had been said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Samādhihastyuttaraśrī, spoke thus to the bodhisattva Vijayavikrāmin:

"Noble son, to the south-west of here, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system named Sahā. There dwells, remains, and maintains himself the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni."
He fully elucidates the perfection of wisdom for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas;
such is his majestic power.
Then, the bodhisattva Vijayavikrāmī addressed the Tathāgata Samādhihastyuttaraśrī in this way:

“Blessed One, I shall go to that Sahā world-system in order to behold, pay homage to, and attend upon that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and those Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who are for the most part youthful, have attained the *dhāraṇīs*, are skilled in the production of *samādhis*, and have reached the perfection of mastery over all *samādhis*.”
The Blessed One said:
"Go, noble son, whenever you deem it the right time.
Then the Tathāgata Samādhihastyuttaraśrī gave to the Bodhisattva Vijayavikrāmin lotuses made of various jewels, shining with gold, each having a thousand petals.
"O son of good family, scatter these lotuses over the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and speak thus:

'The Blessed One Samādhihastyuttaraśrī inquires after your freedom from illness, your freedom from affliction, your lightness of movement, your well-being, your strength, and your dwelling in comfort.'"
And these lotuses have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Samādhihastyuttaraśrī, to the Blessed One.
Furthermore, noble son, may you be one who acts with full awareness in that buddha-field. Why is that?
Because those bodhisattvas who have been born there in this Sahā world-system are difficult to approach.

Then the Bodhisattva Vijayavikrāmin, having taken from the presence of the Tathāgata Samādhihastyuttaraśrī those lotuses made of various jewels, shining like gold and possessing a thousand petals, was surrounded and escorted by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas—
both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls— and departed toward the northeast.
Honoring, revering, respecting, and worshipping the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in every direction—
offering flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards— he arrived at this Sahā world-system.
He approached the place where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha was; having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.

Standing to one side, the Bodhisattva Vijayavikrāmī addressed the Blessed One Śākyamuni as follows: "Blessed One, Samādhisastyuttaraśrī inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, physical ease, well-being, strength, and whether you dwell in comfort."
And these thousand-petaled lotuses, made of various jewels and shining like gold, were sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Samādhihastyuttaraśrī, to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, took those lotuses and cast them toward those world-systems in the northeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā; and by those lotuses, those world-systems became completely filled. And within those lotuses, forms of Buddhas appeared.

And seated in those buddha-fields, they teach the Dharma— namely, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the perfection of wisdom— and those beings by whom that Dharma was heard became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Then indeed, those bodhisattvas, those householders, those renunciants, those boys, and those girls...

Then those maidens, having come from the world-system Samādhyalaṃkṛtā together with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vijayavikrāmin, honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the Blessed One Śākyamuni according to their respective roots of merit, and sat down to one side.

Then, indeed, having passed beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the southeastern direction, there is a world-system situated at the very limit of them called Bodhimaṇḍālaṃkārarucirā; therein dwells, remains, and maintains his life the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Padmottaraśrī.
He teaches this very Dharma of the perfection of wisdom to the bodhisattvas.

Then, in that world-system, a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Padmahasta, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake, and that most beautiful physical form of the Blessed One, [approached him].

He approached the place where the Blessed One Padmottaraśrī, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha was; having approached, he bowed at the feet of that Blessed One and addressed the Tathāgata Padmottaraśrī as follows:
"What, Blessed One, is the cause?"
"What is the cause for the appearance in the world of this great radiance, this great earthquake of the earth, and the manifestation of this most wonderful body of the Tathāgata?
When this was said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Padmottaraśrī, spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Padmahasta:

"Noble son, to the northwest of here, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, there is a world-system called Sahā. There, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni resides, stays, and maintains himself;
he is fully revealing the perfection of wisdom to the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. Such is his majestic power."
Then the Bodhisattva Padmahasta said this to the Tathāgata Padmottaraśrī:
"Blessed One, I shall go to that world-system named Sahā in order to behold that Tathāgata Śākyamuni."

In order to pay homage and attend upon those bodhisattva mahāsattvas— who were for the most part youthful, had attained the dhāraṇīs, were skilled in the production of samādhis, and had reached the perfection of mastery over all samādhis—
that Blessed One said:
"Go, noble son, whenever you deem it the right time.
Then the Tathāgata Padmottaraśrī gave to the Bodhisattva Padmahasta thousand-petaled lotuses made of various jewels and shining with the luster of gold, saying,
"Noble son, with these lotuses you should scatter over that Tathāgata Śākyamuni."
And you should say this:
"The Blessed One Padmottaraśrī inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, ease of movement, vigor, strength, and well-being;
and these lotuses have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened One Padmottaraśrī, to the Blessed One."
"And may you, noble son, be one who acts with full awareness in that buddha-field. Why is that?
Because those bodhisattvas who have been born there in this Sahā world-system are difficult to approach.
Then the bodhisattva Padmahasta, having received from the Tathāgata Padmottaraśrī those lotuses made of various jewels—golden-hued and possessing a thousand petals—departed.

Surrounded and escorted by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas— both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls— he honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in those world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the southeastern direction, with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards.

He arrived at this Sahā world-system and approached the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One; having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.
Standing to one side with a lotus in his hand, the Bodhisattva addressed the Blessed One Śākyamuni as follows:
"The Blessed One Padmottaraśrī inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, ease of movement, vigor, strength, and well-being.
Furthermore, the Tathāgata Padmottaraśrī has sent these thousand-petaled lotuses, made of various jewels and shining like gold, to the Blessed One."
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, took those lotuses and cast them toward those world-systems in the southeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā;
by those lotuses, those world-systems were completely filled.

And upon those lotuses sat forms of the Buddha, and in those buddha-fields they taught the Dharma— namely, this very teaching of the Dharma connected with the perfection of wisdom— and those beings by whom that Dharma was heard became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Then indeed, those bodhisattvas, those householders, those renunciants, those boys, and those girls...

Then those maidens, together with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmahasta from the world-system Surucirā, which is adorned for the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), arrived; having honored, revered, respected, and worshiped the Blessed One Śākyamuni with their respective roots of merit, they sat down to one side.

Then, indeed, having passed beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the southwestern direction, there is a world-system at the very limit of them called Vigataraja-sañcaya; therein dwells, remains, and maintains his life the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Sūryamaṇḍalaprabhāsottamaśrī.
He teaches this very Dharma of the perfection of wisdom to the bodhisattvas.

Then, in that world-system, a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Sūryaprabhāsa, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake, and having seen that most beautiful body of the Blessed One, [approached him].
He approached the place where the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sūryamaṇḍalaprabhāsottamaśrī was staying;
having approached and bowed at the feet of that Blessed One, he addressed the Tathāgata Sūryamaṇḍalaprabhāsottamaśrī as follows:
"What, Blessed One, is the cause?"
"What is the cause for the appearance of this great radiance in the world, for this great earthquake of the earth, and for the manifestation of this most wonderful body of a Tathāgata?
When this was said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sūryamaṇḍalaprabhāsottamaśrī, spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Sūryaprabhāsa:

"Noble son, there is, in the northeastern direction, beyond worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, a world-system named Sahā. There, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni resides, stays, and maintains his life;
he is fully revealing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) to the bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and such is his majestic power."

Then the bodhisattva Sūryaprabhāsa said this to the Tathāgata Sūryamaṇḍalaprabhāsottamaśrī: "Blessed One, I shall go to that Sahā world-system in order to see, pay homage to, and attend upon that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are for the most part youthful."
They had attained the dhāraṇīs, were skilled in the production of meditative concentrations, and had reached the perfection of mastery over all samādhis.
The Blessed One said:
"Go, noble son, whenever you deem it the right time."
Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Sūryamaṇḍalaprabhāsottamaśrī gave to the Bodhisattva Sūryaprabhā lotuses made of various jewels, shining with gold, each having a thousand petals,
saying: "O son of good family, with these lotuses you should scatter over that Tathāgata Śākyamuni,
and you should speak thus:"
The Blessed One Sūryamaṇḍalaprabhāsottamaśrī inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, ease of movement, vigor, strength, and dwelling in comfort.
These lotuses have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Sūryamaṇḍalaprabhāsottamaśrī, to the Blessed One.
Furthermore, O son of good family, may you be one who acts with full awareness in that Buddha-field. For what reason?
For those bodhisattvas who have been born there in that Sahā world-system are indeed difficult to approach.

Then, the bodhisattva Sūryaprabhāsa, having taken from the presence of the Tathāgata Sūryamaṇḍalaprabhāsottamaśrī those lotuses made of various jewels, which were golden-hued and possessed a thousand petals, together with many others...

Surrounded and escorted by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas— both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls— he proceeded toward the southwestern direction, honoring, revering, respecting, and worshipping the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in those world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards.
He arrived at this Sahā world-system and approached where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni was;
having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.
Standing to one side, the Bodhisattva Sūryaprabhāsa addressed the Blessed One Śākyamuni as follows:
"The Blessed One Sūryamaṇḍalaprabhāsottamaśrī inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, ease of movement, vigor, strength, and well-being;
he inquires after these things. (PvsP1-1: 21)
And by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Sūryamaṇḍalaprabhāsottamaśrī, lotuses made of various jewels, shining with the luster of gold and possessing a thousand petals, were sent to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, took those lotuses and cast them toward those world-systems in the southwestern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā;
and by those lotuses, those world-systems became completely filled.

And upon those lotuses sat forms of the Buddha, and in those buddha-fields they taught the Dharma— namely, this very teaching of the Dharma connected with the perfection of wisdom— and those beings by whom that Dharma was heard became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Then indeed, those bodhisattvas, those householders, those renunciants, those boys, and those...

Then those maidens, together with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sūryaprabha from the world-system Vigatarajaḥsañcaya, arrived; having honored, revered, respected, and worshiped the Blessed One Śākyamuni with their respective roots of merit, they sat down to one side.

Then, indeed, having passed beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the northwestern direction, there is a world-system that is the very last of them called Vaśībhūta; therein dwells, remains, and maintains his life a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Ekacchattra.
He taught this very Perfection of Wisdom as the Dharma for the Bodhisattvas.

Then, in that world-system, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Ratnottama, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake, and that most wonderful physical form of the Blessed One, [was filled with wonder].

He approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened one, Ekacchattra; having approached and bowed at the feet of that Blessed One, he said this to the Tathāgata Ekacchattra:
"What, Blessed One, is the cause?"
What is the cause for the appearance of this great radiance in the world,
and for the manifestation of this great earthquake and this most wonderful manifestation of the Tathāgata’s own body?
When this had been said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ekacchattra, spoke thus to the bodhisattva Ratnottama:

"Noble son, to the southeast of here, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system named Sahā. There, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni dwells, remains, and sustains himself."
He reveals the perfection of wisdom to the bodhisattvas, the great beings; such is his majestic power.
Then the bodhisattva Ratnottama said this to the Tathāgata Ekacchattra:
"Blessed One, I shall go to that Sahā world-system in order to behold that Tathāgata Śākyamuni."

In order to pay homage and attend upon those bodhisattva mahāsattvas— who for the most part were youthful, had attained dhāraṇīs, were skilled in the production of samādhis, and had reached the perfection of mastery over all samādhis—
that Blessed One said:
"Go, noble son, at whatever time you deem appropriate.
Then the Tathāgata Ekacchattra gave to the Bodhisattva Ratnottama lotuses made of various jewels, shining with gold and having a thousand petals, saying:
"Noble son, with these lotuses you should scatter over that Tathāgata Śākyamuni."
And you should say this:
"The Blessed One Ekacchattra inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, ease of movement, vigor, strength, and well-being;
and these lotuses have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One Ekacchattra, to the Blessed One."
And may you, noble son, be one who acts with clear comprehension in that buddha-field. Why is that?
For those bodhisattvas who have been born there in this Sahā world-system are difficult to approach.
Then the bodhisattva Ratnottama, from the presence of the Tathāgata Ekacchattra, [received] those various objects made of jewels...

Holding lotuses that shone like gold and had a thousand petals, he was surrounded and escorted by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas— both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls— and while honoring and revering the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in those world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the northwestern direction, he proceeded.
Honoring and worshipping with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, flags, and victory standards,
he arrived at this Sahā world-system and approached the place where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, was staying.
Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he stood to one side; and standing to one side, the bodhisattva Ratnottama addressed the Blessed One Śākyamuni as follows:
The Blessed One Ekacchattra inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, ease of movement, well-being, strength, and whether he dwells in comfort;
and these thousand-petaled lotuses made of various jewels and shining with gold have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ekacchattra, to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, took those lotuses and cast them toward those world-systems in the northwestern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.
Those world-systems became filled with those lotuses,
and within those lotuses sat forms of Buddhas who taught the Dharma in those Buddha-fields— namely, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the perfection of wisdom.
And those beings who heard that Dharma became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Then indeed, those bodhisattvas, those householders, those renunciants, those boys,
and those girls [departed] from that world-system Vaśībhūtā together with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Ratnottama.

Having arrived with their respective roots of merit, they honored, revered, respected, and worshiped the Blessed One Śākyamuni, and then sat down to one side. Then, having passed beyond world-systems in the direction below as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, from among those [world-systems], there was one that was the very last.
In that world-system named Padmā, there dwells, remains, and maintains himself a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Padmaśrī;
he teaches this very Perfection of Wisdom as the Dharma for Bodhisattvas.
Now, in that world-system, there was a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Padmottara who [beheld] that great radiance.
Having seen that great earthquake and having beheld the unsurpassable physical form of the Blessed One,

he approached where the Blessed One Padmaśrī, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha was; having approached and bowed at the feet of that Blessed One, he addressed the Tathāgata Padmaśrī as follows:
"Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition,
for the manifestation of this great radiance in the world?"
"And it is for the sake of manifesting this great earthquake and this most beautiful body of the Tathāgata.
When this had been said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Padmaśrī, spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Padmottara:

"Noble son, there is, in the direction above, beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, a world-system named Sahā; there dwells a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni."
He stands, remains, and continues to live;
he reveals the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) of the bodhisattvas, the great beings (*mahāsattvas*), and such is his majestic power.
Then, the bodhisattva Padmottara said this to the Tathāgata Padmaśrī:
"Blessed One, I shall go to that Sahā world-system to behold, pay homage to, and attend upon that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and those Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who for the most part are youthful,
have attained the dhāraṇīs, are skilled in the production of samādhis, and have reached the perfection of mastery over all samādhis."
The Blessed One said:
"Go, noble son, at whatever time you deem appropriate.
Then the Tathāgata Padmaśrī gave to the Bodhisattva Padmottara lotuses made of various jewels, shining with gold and having a thousand petals.
"O son of good family, scatter these lotuses over that Tathāgata Śākyamuni and speak thus:
'The Blessed One Padmaśrī inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, vigor, well-being, strength, and whether he dwells in comfort.'"
"These lotuses have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmaśrī, to the Blessed One.
Furthermore, noble son, may you be one who acts with full awareness in that buddha-field. Why is that?
Because those bodhisattvas who have been born there in this Sahā world-system are difficult to approach."

Then indeed, the Bodhisattva Padmottara, having taken from the presence of the Tathāgata Padmaśrī those lotuses made of various jewels, shining like gold and possessing a thousand petals, was surrounded and escorted by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas— both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls— as he proceeded below.

Honoring, revering, respecting, and worshiping the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in every direction— with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards— he arrived at this Sahā world system and approached the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One.
Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he stood to one side.

Standing to one side, the Bodhisattva Padmottara addressed the Blessed One Śākyamuni as follows: "The Blessed One Padmaśrī inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from affliction, freedom from illness, ease of movement, well-being, strength, and whether you dwell in comfort."

And these lotuses made of various jewels, shining with the luster of gold and possessing a thousand petals, were sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Padmaśrī, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, took those lotuses and cast them toward those world-systems in the direction below, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā;
and by those lotuses, those world-systems became completely filled.
And upon those lotuses sat forms of the Buddha,

and in those buddha-fields they taught the Dharma— namely, this very teaching of the Dharma connected with the perfection of wisdom— and those beings by whom that Dharma was heard became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Then indeed those bodhisattvas— those householders, those renunciants, those boys, and those girls—

who had come from that world-system Padmā together with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Padmottara, having honored, revered, respected, and worshiped the Blessed One Śākyamuni with their respective roots of merit, sat down to one side.
Then, indeed, having passed beyond world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the direction above, there is a world-system at the very limit of all those, named Nandā.
There, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Nandaśrī resides, stays, and maintains himself;
he teaches this very Prajñāpāramitā as the Dharma for Bodhisattvas.
Then, indeed, in that world-system, the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Nandadatta, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake,
and having seen the unsurpassed physical form of the Blessed One, approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Nandaśrī.
Having approached and bowed at the feet of that Blessed One, he addressed the Tathāgata Nandaśrī as follows:
"O Blessed One, what is the cause? What is the condition for the manifestation of this great radiance in the world?"
"And this is for the sake of manifesting this great earthquake and this most beautiful body of the Tathāgata.
When this had been said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Nandaśrī, spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Nandadatta:

"Noble son, below from here, after crossing world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, there is a world-system named Sahā; there dwells the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śākyamuni."
He remains, stays, and maintains himself;
he thoroughly elucidates the *prajñāpāramitā* of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas—such is his majestic power. Then, the bodhisattva Nandadatta said this to the Tathāgata Nandaśrī:
"Blessed One, I shall go to that Sahā world-system to behold, pay homage to, and attend upon that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and those Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who for the most part are youthful,
have attained the dhāraṇīs, are skilled in the production of meditative absorptions, and have reached the perfection of mastery over all samādhis."
The Blessed One said:
"Go, noble son, whenever you deem it the right time.
Then the Tathāgata Nandaśrī gave to the bodhisattva Nandadatta thousand-petaled lotuses made of various jewels and radiant with gold.
"Son of good family, scatter these lotuses over that Tathāgata Śākyamuni and speak thus:
'The Blessed One Nandaśrī inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from affliction, freedom from illness, lightness of body, vigor, well-being, strength, and comfortable dwelling.'"
"And these lotuses have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Nandaśrī, to the Blessed One.
Furthermore, noble son, may you be one who acts with full awareness in that buddhafield. Why is that?
For those bodhisattvas who have been born there in this Sahā world-system are difficult to approach."

Then the Bodhisattva Nandadatta, having taken from the presence of the Tathāgata Nandaśrī those lotuses made of various jewels, shining like gold and possessing a thousand petals, was surrounded and escorted by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas— both householders and renunciants, as well as boys and girls— as he proceeded above.

In those world-systems in every direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, he honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards.

He arrived at this Sahā world-system and approached the place where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, was staying; having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.
Standing to one side, the bodhisattva Nandadatta addressed the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, as follows:
"The Blessed One Nandaśrī inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from affliction, freedom from illness, ease of movement, well-being, strength, and dwelling in comfort;

and these thousand-petaled lotuses, made of various jewels and shining with the luster of gold, have been sent by that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Nandaśrī, to the Blessed One."
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, took those lotuses and cast them toward those world-systems in the direction above that are as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.
Those world-systems became filled with those lotuses,
and within those lotuses sat forms of Buddhas who taught the Dharma in those Buddha-fields— namely, this very teaching of the Dharma associated with the perfection of wisdom.
And those beings who heard that Dharma became fixed in their destiny for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Then indeed, those bodhisattvas, those householders, those renunciants, those boys,
and those girls came from that world-system Nanda together with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Nandadatta.
Having honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the Blessed One Śākyamuni with their respective roots of merit, they sat down to one side.
Then, in that very instant, moment, and second, this great trichiliocosm world-system became composed of the seven precious gems and strewn with flowers;

it was draped with bundles of silk ribbons and streamers, and adorned by *kalpa*-trees whose branches were bent low with various ornaments as fruit, as well as by flowering trees, fruit trees, fragrant trees, and garland trees.

It was just as if the Blessed One had beheld the world-system Padmāvatī, the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Samantakusuma, where Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta dwells, along with Susthitamati and other bodhisattvas of great and small majesty.

The world with its gods, its Māras, and its Brahmās; this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods, humans, and asuras—all were assembled there, as were those bodhisattvas who had become youths.
This was the introduction.
Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Śāriputra:
"Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully awaken to all phenomena in all their aspects should apply himself to the perfection of wisdom.
Thus, in brief, the production of the thought of enlightenment is accompanied by the desire for perfect awakening.
When this had been said, the venerable Śāriputra addressed the Blessed One as follows:
“Blessed One, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully awaken to all phenomena in all their aspects apply himself to the perfection of wisdom?
When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Śāriputra:
“In this regard, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, standing in the perfection of wisdom by way of the yoga of non-abiding, [should so apply himself].”

The perfection of generosity is to be fulfilled by means of non-renunciation, based on the non-apprehension of the gift, the giver, and the recipient; the perfection of ethical discipline is to be fulfilled based on the state of neither transgression nor non-transgression nor the committing of a transgression;
the perfection of patience is to be fulfilled based on the state of being unshakeable.
The perfection of vigor is to be fulfilled by means of the non-laxity of physical and mental vigor;
the perfection of meditation is to be fulfilled by means of non-savoring;
the perfection of wisdom is to be fulfilled by means of the non-apprehension of wisdom and lack of wisdom.
Thus, in detail, is the production of the thought of enlightenment accompanied by the desire for awakening.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva who wishes to lead all those beings in each of the worlds in the ten directions— worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges— to final nirvana in the realm of nirvana without remainder, [should produce that thought].
A mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Thus, in brief, the production of the thought [of awakening] has as its objective the welfare of others;
likewise, for one who desires to establish in generosity those beings who are miserly, in ethical discipline those who are immoral, and in patience those who abound in malice—

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish those who are lazy in vigor, those with distracted minds in meditative concentration, and those with impaired wisdom in the perfection of wisdom should train in the perfection of wisdom.
This is the generation of the mind of awakening (cittotpāda) in detail as having the welfare of others as its objective support.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fully awaken to all phenomena in all their aspects should abide in the perfection of wisdom.

Thus, accompanied by aspiration and like the earth, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having thus stood in the perfection of wisdom by means of the yoga of non-abiding, should fulfill the perfection of generosity through the non-apprehension of the gift, the giver, and the recipient.

In this way, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom are to be fulfilled by means of the non-apprehension of wisdom and lack of wisdom.
Thus, accompanied by such an intention and resembling fine gold,
Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, remaining thus in the perfection of wisdom, must fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness.
The four right efforts, the four bases of miraculous power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the noble eightfold path must be fulfilled;
the concentration on emptiness must be cultivated,
and the concentration on the signless must be cultivated.
The concentration of wishlessness (apraṇihita-samādhi) should be cultivated;

likewise, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables (apramāṇa), the four formless attainments (ārūpya-samāpatti), the eight liberations (vimokṣa), the nine successive meditative attainments (anupūrva-vihāra-samāpatti), and the nine perceptions of the foul (aśubha-saṃjñā) should be cultivated. What are the nine?

Namely, one should cultivate the perception of a bloated corpse, the perception of a fissured corpse, the perception of a festering corpse, the perception of a bloody corpse, the perception of a livid corpse, the perception of a gnawed corpse, the perception of a scattered corpse, the perception of a skeletal corpse, the perception of a burnt corpse,
and the perception of repulsiveness toward food; furthermore, the recollection of the Buddha should be cultivated.
The recollection of the Dharma should be cultivated; the recollection of the Saṅgha should be cultivated;
the recollection of ethical discipline should be cultivated.
The recollection of relinquishment should be cultivated; the recollection of the deities should be cultivated; the recollection of mindfulness of breathing should be cultivated.
The recollection of agitation should be cultivated; the recollection of death should be cultivated;
the perception of impermanence should be cultivated.
The perception of suffering should be cultivated; the perception of non-self should be cultivated;
the perception of impurity should be cultivated.
The perception of death should be cultivated; the perception of non-delight in the entire world should be cultivated;
the perception of lack of trust in the entire world should be cultivated.
The perception of thorough mastery should be cultivated; the perception of conventional reality should be cultivated;
the perception of things according to their literal expression should be cultivated.
Concentration with applied thought and sustained thought should be cultivated;
concentration without applied thought and with sustained thought only should be cultivated.
The concentration without applied thought and without sustained thought should be cultivated;
the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" should be cultivated;
the faculty of "knowing" should be cultivated.
The faculty of one who has already known should be cultivated; the bases of mastery should be cultivated; the bases of totality should be cultivated.
The knowledge of an omniscient one should be cultivated; calm abiding and insight should be cultivated;
the three types of higher knowledge should be cultivated; and the four analytical knowledges should be cultivated.
The four grounds of self-confidence should be cultivated;
the five unshakable higher knowledges should be cultivated;
the six perfections should be cultivated.
The seven riches are to be cultivated;
the eight thoughts of a great person are to be cultivated;
the ten powers of a Tathāgata are to be cultivated.
The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha should be cultivated;
great loving-kindness should be cultivated;
great compassion should be cultivated.
Great sympathetic joy should be cultivated; great equanimity should be cultivated.
Thus, accompanied by resolute intention, he is like the new moon.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to transcend omniscience by means of knowledge and vision,

who wishes to fulfill the knowledge of the path, who wishes to attain the knowledge of all aspects, who wishes to fulfill the aspect of knowing the mental activities of all sentient beings, and who wishes to uproot all afflictions along with their latencies and habitual tendencies, must cultivate the perfection of wisdom.
One should apply oneself to the perfection of wisdom. Thus should a bodhisattva mahāsattva train in the perfection of wisdom:

one who desires to enter the fixed course of a bodhisattva, one who desires to transcend the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, one who desires to stand upon the stage of non-retrogression, and one who desires to completely transcend the stage of a youth.

One who desires to attain the six superknowledges (*ṣaḍ-abhijñā*), one who desires to know the movements and fluctuations of the minds and conduct of all sentient beings, and one who desires to surpass the knowledge of all *śrāvakas* and *pratyekabuddhas*, should apply themselves to the "entrance of the dhāraṇī-samādhi. This practice is like a blazing fire. Furthermore, one who desires to establish stingy sentient beings in generosity, and who desires to give gifts to all *śrāvakas* and *pratyekabuddhas*...
A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to surpass those gifts being given by means of a single thought-moment accompanied by rejoicing should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Thus, that which is accompanied by the perfection of giving is like a great treasure-store.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish those of immoral conduct in morality, and who wishes to surpass the morality of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas with a single thought-moment accompanied by sympathetic joy, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Thus, that which is associated with the perfection of morality is like a mine of jewels.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish those with malicious minds in patience, and who wishes to surpass the patience of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas by means of a single thought-moment accompanied by sympathetic joy, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Thus is the state associated with patience, which is like a great ocean.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish the indolent in vigor, and who wishes to surpass the vigor of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas with a single thought-moment accompanied by rejoicing, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Thus is the diamond-like [samādhi] accompanied by vigor.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish those with distracted minds in meditative concentration, and who wishes to surpass the meditative concentrations of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas by means of a single thought-moment accompanied by sympathetic joy, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Thus is the simile of the mountain associated with the perfection of meditative concentration.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish beings of poor wisdom in wisdom, and who wishes to surpass the wisdom of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas with a single thought-moment accompanied by rejoicing,
should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Thus, accompanied by wisdom and resembling a great medicine,

a bodhisattva mahāsattva— who, through skill in means, desires to render even a single arising of a wholesome thought immeasurable and incalculable in terms of omniscience by way of dedication— should, while giving even a small gift, practice the perfection of wisdom.
By one who guards even a small amount of ethical discipline,
cultivates even a small amount of patience,
and exerts even a small amount of vigor;

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to perform what is immeasurable and incalculable by dedicating even a small amount of meditative concentration and a small amount of wisdom toward the knowledge of all aspects for the sake of all sentient beings through skill in means,
should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of generosity must train in the perfection of wisdom;

likewise, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of ethical discipline, practicing the perfection of patience, practicing the perfection of vigor, practicing the perfection of meditative concentration, and practicing the perfection of wisdom must train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to endure the sufferings of the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama for the sake of all sentient beings; who wishes to relinquish even the morality accumulated over hundreds of thousands of eons out of neglect toward sentient beings; and who wishes to bring to perfection the eighty minor marks and the thirty-two marks of a great man within the family of the Buddhas—such a bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Thus, it is accompanied by skillful means and is like a friend.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to bring the Buddha-body to completion should train in the perfection of wisdom;
