a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to ascend to the stage of a youth (kumārabhūmi) should train in the perfection of wisdom;
and a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes never to be separated from the Buddhas and bodhisattvas should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to make himself known with a single voice throughout world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the eastern direction should train in the perfection of wisdom. Likewise,

one who wishes to make himself known with a single voice throughout world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the southern, western, northern, intermediate directions, below, and above should train in the perfection of wisdom.
One should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to remain so that the lineage of the Three Jewels is not interrupted should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should [train] with whichever roots of merit he desires.

"A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: 'May these various roots of merit of mine flourish so that I may honor, revere, respect, and worship the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Thus, it is accompanied by aspiration and is like a wish-fulfilling gem."

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to fulfill the desires of all sentient beings with such requisites as food, drink, clothing, perfumes, garlands, flowers, incense, powders, ointments, beds, seats, houses, wealth, grain, ornaments, jewels, gems, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, gold, silver, gardens, kingdoms, and so forth, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish all sentient beings— in a world that is bounded by the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) and terminates at the realm of space (*ākāśadhātu*)— in the perfection of generosity, and who wishes to establish them in the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to make even a single arising of a wholesome thought inexhaustible until the final awakening at the seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "May the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the ten directions, speak my praises.
Thus is the simile of the sun associated with power.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to train in internal emptiness should train in the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, he should train in external emptiness,
internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, and unconditioned emptiness.

A bodhisattva who wishes to train in ultimate emptiness, beginningless and endless emptiness, non-dispersal emptiness, natural emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of the unapprehendable, the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, the emptiness of existence, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of extrinsic nature— by such a bodhisattva [should this be studied].
A mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to realize the suchness of all phenomena (sarvadharma-tathatā) should train in the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, a bodhisattva who wishes to realize the suchness of the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu-tathatā) [should train in the perfection of wisdom].
A great being must train in the perfection of wisdom;

a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to realize the suchness of the limit of all that exists must train in the perfection of wisdom. It is in this way, Śāriputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva must train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to know all the atoms of earth, water, fire, and wind within the triple-thousand great thousandfold world-system should practice the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom knows that giving a gift in this way results in great fruit;
he knows that giving a gift in this way causes one to be reborn in the great kṣatriya clans.
He causes [beings] to be reborn in great brahmin families, he causes them to be reborn in great householder families;
likewise, this gift given causes them to be reborn among the gods of the Four Great Kings.
In this way, giving such a gift causes one to be reborn among the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three;
in this way, giving such a gift causes one to be reborn among the Yāma gods; in this way, giving such a gift causes one to be reborn among the Tuṣita gods.
Giving in this manner leads to rebirth among the Nirmāṇarati gods;
giving in this manner leads to rebirth among the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods; and giving in this manner conduces to the attainment of the first dhyāna.
Giving gifts in this way conduces to the attainment of the second dhyāna;
giving gifts in this way conduces to the attainment of the third dhyāna;
giving gifts in this way conduces to the attainment of the fourth dhyāna.

Thus, giving such a gift conduces to the attainment of the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite consciousness; thus, giving such a gift conduces to the attainment of the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space;
thus, giving such a gift conduces to the attainment of the meditative absorption of the sphere of nothingness.
Giving given in this way leads to the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;
giving given in this way leads to the attainment of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment;
giving given in this way leads to the attainment of the fruit of stream-entry.

Thus, giving such a gift conduces to the attainment of the fruit of once-returning; thus, giving such a gift conduces to the attainment of the fruit of non-returning; thus, giving such a gift conduces to the attainment of the fruit of arhatship.
In this way, giving such a gift conduces to the attainment of the state of a Pratyekabuddha; in this way, giving such a gift conduces to the attainment of the state of a Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should know this:
Thus, giving with skillful means fulfills the perfection of generosity; thus, giving fulfills the perfection of ethical discipline; thus, giving [fulfills the other perfections].
Giving thus fulfills the perfection of patience; giving thus fulfills the perfection of vigor;
giving thus fulfills the perfection of meditative concentration.
"In this way, giving a gift fulfills the perfection of wisdom.
When this had been said, the venerable Śāriputra addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"Blessed One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while giving a gift, fulfill the perfection of generosity?"
How is the perfection of ethical discipline fulfilled by one giving a gift?
How is the perfection of patience fulfilled by one giving a gift?
How is the perfection of vigor fulfilled by one giving a gift?
"How is it that the perfection of meditation is fulfilled by one giving a gift?
How, Blessed One, is the perfection of wisdom fulfilled by a bodhisattva mahāsattva while giving a gift?
The Blessed One said:
Through non-apprehension of the gift, the giver, and the recipient, the perfection of generosity is fulfilled;
through the state of neither transgression nor non-transgression, the perfection of ethical discipline is fulfilled;
and through being unshakeable and not causing agitation, the perfection of patience is fulfilled.
Through the non-laxity of physical and mental vigor, the perfection of vigor is fulfilled;
by means of non-distraction and non-conceptualization, the perfection of meditation is fulfilled;
and through the yoga of non-apprehension while discerning all phenomena, the perfection of wisdom is fulfilled.
In this way, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives a gift, all six perfections are fulfilled;
likewise, within the perfection of ethical discipline, all six perfections are fulfilled;
likewise, within the perfection of patience, all six perfections are fulfilled.
In this way, within the perfection of vigor, all six perfections are fulfilled;
in this way, within the perfection of meditation, all six perfections are fulfilled;
and in this way, within the perfection of wisdom, all six perfections are fulfilled.
Thus, accompanied by wisdom and resembling the sound of sweet music,

furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who, with a single production of the thought of awakening, desires to traverse world-systems in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—

and likewise in the southern, western, northern, intermediate directions, below, and above, in every quarter, desiring to traverse world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges— by that bodhisattva mahāsattva...
One should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, whatever mass of water there is in the great oceans, in the great rivers, small streams, springs, lakes, ponds, and pools within the triple-thousand great-thousand world system— all that [water], with [a vessel] split into a hundred parts...
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to lift up [the world-system] with the tip of a single hair and yet does not wish to harm the living beings dependent upon it,
should train in the perfection of wisdom. Moreover, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva [who wishes to do so regarding] the trichiliocosm...
A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to extinguish with a single breath from his mouth the fire blazing at the end of an aeon should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva [should train] regarding the whirlwind of the agitating wind-circle at the time of the world’s destruction by wind.

One who wishes to cover with the tip of a single finger-joint that whirlwind-circle of agitation which, while currently blowing, shakes, scatters, and pulverizes all mountains— including Sumeru, Mahāsumeru, Cakravāḍa, and Mahācakravāḍa— as well as the entire great earth,
should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to pervade the entire realm of space within the trichiliocosm great thousandfold world system with a single cross-legged posture should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva [who wishes to do so] within the trichiliocosm great thousandfold world system...

One should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "May I bind together Sumeru, Mahāsumeru, Cakravāḍa, Mahācakravāḍa, and other such mountains with a single hair, and cause them to pass beyond, or cast them into, incalculable and immeasurable world-systems.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva [should train] regarding each and every buddha-field in the ten directions.

One who wishes to see the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, with the divine eye; who wishes to hear their teaching of the Dharma with the divine ear; who wishes to know the mental activities of all sentient beings; who wishes to recollect their former abodes;
who wishes to bring forth the superknowledge of the knowledge of the destruction of the outflows; and who wishes to realize the limit of reality, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Thus, endowed with the superknowledges, he is like a great king.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to provide for, with a single alms-bowl, as many Blessed Buddhas together with their assemblies of śrāvakas and bodhisattvas as there are in each of the ten directions in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—

One should train in the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, one who wishes to honor, revere, respect, and worship those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly enlightened Buddhas with clouds of flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, and flags should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish all those beings in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the eastern direction within the aggregate of ethical discipline, the aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation—
by one desiring to establish [beings] in the fruit of stream-entry,
by one desiring to establish them in the fruit of once-returning,
and by one desiring to establish them in the fruit of non-returning;
One who wishes to establish beings in arhatship, one who wishes to establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment, and so on up to establishing them in the realm of nirvana without remainder,
should train in the perfection of wisdom. As it is in the eastern direction, so it is in the southern, western, and northern directions.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish all sentient beings— in each of the world systems in the intermediate directions, below, and above, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā— within the realm of nirvana without remainder, must train in the perfection of wisdom.
Thus, accompanied by merit and knowledge, it is like a storehouse.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to attain the qualities of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to go to the further shore of conditioned and unconditioned phenomena should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva [who wishes to understand] all phenomena of the past, future, and present...
One who desires to awaken to the Tathāgatas and desires to reach the limit of non-arising (*anutpāda-koṭi*) of all phenomena should train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
Thus, it is like a great highway accompanied by the factors conducive to awakening (*bodhipakṣa*).
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who desires to become a leader for all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas should [train] in the perfection of wisdom.
One must train.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to become an attendant to the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to become a member of the inner retinue of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to have a great retinue, and who wishes to obtain a retinue of bodhisattvas, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to purify their offerings should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to subdue the mind of stinginess should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes not to give rise to a mind of immorality should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes not to give rise to a mind of malice should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon a mind of laziness should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to abandon a distracted mind should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to prevent a mind of poor wisdom from proliferating should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish all sentient beings in the bases of meritorious action consisting of giving should [train in the perfection of wisdom].
One who wishes to establish others in the basis of meritorious action consisting of morality,

one who wishes to establish them in the basis of meritorious action consisting of cultivation, and one who wishes to establish them in the basis of meritorious action consisting of material things accompanied by service, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to produce the five eyes should train in the perfection of wisdom. What are the five?
Namely, one who wishes to produce the fleshly eye, the divine eye, the wisdom eye, the dharma eye, and the buddha eye should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to see with the divine eye as many Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā in the eastern direction, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Likewise, one who wishes to see with the divine eye as many Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā in the southern direction should train in the perfection of wisdom.
One who wishes to see with the divine eye as many Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā in the western direction should train in the perfection of wisdom.
One who wishes to see, with the divine eye, Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the northern direction, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
One who wishes to see, with the divine eye, Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the northeastern direction, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
One who wishes to see, with the divine eye, Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the southeastern direction, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
One who wishes to see, with the divine eye, Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the southwestern direction, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
One who wishes to see, with the divine eye, Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the northwestern direction, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
One who wishes to see, with the divine eye, Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the downward direction, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
One who, with the divine eye, desires to see the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the direction above—numbering as many as the sands of the river Ganges—should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, one who desires to hear with the divine ear those teachings which those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, proclaim;
and one who desires to understand, as they truly are, the minds of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, by means of their own mind, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
One who wishes to recollect the state of bodhisattvahood associated with the former lives of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones,

and one who wishes to behold the miraculous transformations of the supernatural powers (*ṛddhi-vikurvita*) of those Buddhas, should train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva [should train] in the perfection of wisdom in order to hear the teachings that those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are proclaiming throughout all world-systems in the ten directions.

Having heard them, one who wishes to retain them all through an unbreakable reinforcement of the power of mindfulness, until one has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to see the buddha-fields of the past Blessed Buddhas,
and who wishes to see the buddha-fields of the future Blessed Buddhas as well, [should train] in the perfection of wisdom.

One should train. Furthermore, those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who currently reside, remain, and maintain themselves throughout the worlds of the ten directions—by one who wishes to see the Buddha-fields of those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, one should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Thus, accompanied by calm abiding and insight, it is like a vehicle.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the ten directions— namely, the discourses (sūtra), verses in prose and verse (geya), prophecies (vyākaraṇa), stanzas (gāthā), inspired utterances (udāna), introductory narratives (nidāna), historical accounts (itivṛttaka), birth stories (jātaka), extensive teachings (vaipulya), marvelous events (adbhutadharma), parables (avadāna), and instructions (upadeśa)—

a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to take up all of that which has not been heard by the śrāvakas, who wishes to retain it, who wishes to recite it, and who wishes to practice in accordance with suchness, [should train in this perfection of wisdom].
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to reveal this in detail to others should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Moreover, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to take up and retain everything that has been spoken, is being spoken, and will be spoken by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the eastern direction should train in the perfection of wisdom.
One who desires to recite it, who desires to practice for the sake of suchness, and who desires to reveal it in detail to others,
should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the southern direction— [all that is contained therein].
One who wishes to take up all of that, to retain it, to recite it, to practice in accordance with suchness, and to reveal it in detail to others, should train in the perfection of wisdom—
whatever has been spoken or is being spoken by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the western direction.
And one who wishes to speak all that, or who wishes to take it up, retain it, recite it, practice in accordance with suchness, and reveal it in detail to others—
such a person should train in the perfection of wisdom.
This applies to whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the northern direction.
One who wishes to take up all of that, to retain it, to recite it, to practice it in accordance with suchness, and to reveal it in detail to others, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Whatever has been taught, is being taught, or will be taught by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the northeastern direction— [all that one should learn].
One who wishes to take up all that, retain it, recite it, practice it in accordance with suchness, and reveal it in detail to others, should train in the perfection of wisdom—
whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the southeastern direction.
One who wishes to take up all of that, to retain it, to recite it, to practice it in accordance with suchness, and to reveal it in detail to others, should train in the perfection of wisdom—
whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the southern and western directions.
One who wishes to take up all of that, to retain it, to recite it, to practice it in accordance with suchness, and to reveal it in detail to others— should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the northwestern direction.
Furthermore, one who wishes to take up, retain, recite, practice in accordance with reality,
and extensively proclaim to others all that has been, is being, and will be spoken by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the direction below, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

All that— whatever has been, is being, and will be spoken by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the direction below— one who wishes to take it up, retain it, and recite it [should train in the perfection of wisdom].
One who wishes to practice for the sake of suchness, and who wishes to proclaim it in detail to others, should train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, one who wishes to take up, retain,

and recite everything that has been spoken, is being spoken, or will be spoken by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the upward direction, and who wishes to practice for the sake of suchness, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
And one who wishes to reveal it in detail to others should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Thus, endowed with mnemonic formulas and eloquence, it is like a flowing spring.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, by a bodhisattva mahāsattva, those regions in the eastern direction—in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—that are shrouded in blinding darkness, [should be illuminated].
One who wishes to illuminate all those places where even the light of the sun and moon has no reach should train in the perfection of wisdom.
This applies to those regions in the southern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, which are shrouded in blinding darkness.

One who wishes to illuminate all those places where even the light of the sun and moon has no reach— those regions of blinding darkness in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the western direction— should train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to illuminate all those places where even the light of the sun and moon has no reach— those regions of blinding darkness in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the northern direction— should train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to illuminate all those places where even the light of the sun and moon has no reach— those regions of blinding darkness in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the northeastern direction— should train in the perfection of wisdom.
One who wishes to illuminate all those places where even the light of the sun and moon has no reach should train in the perfection of wisdom.
This applies to those regions in the southeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, which are shrouded in blinding darkness.
One who wishes to illuminate all those places where even the light of the sun and moon has no reach should train in the perfection of wisdom.
This applies to those worlds in the southwestern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, which are shrouded in blinding darkness.

One who wishes to illuminate all those world systems in the northwestern direction— numbering as many as the sands of the river Ganges— in which even the light of the sun and moon has no reach, should train in the perfection of wisdom.
One who wishes to illuminate all those places shrouded in blinding darkness, where even the light of the sun and moon has no reach, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to illuminate all those regions in the downward direction— in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges that are shrouded in blinding darkness, where even the light of the sun and moon has no reach— should train in the perfection of wisdom.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to illuminate all those regions in the upward direction— world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges that are shrouded in blinding darkness, where even the light of the sun and moon does not reach— should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to cause all those beings— who have been born in various buddhafields within the world systems of the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges— to hear the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, and the sound of the Saṅgha;
And one who wishes to establish those beings in right view should train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to cause all those beings born in various Buddha-fields throughout world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the southern direction to hear the sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," and the sound of "Saṃgha," and to establish those beings in right view, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to cause all those beings born in various Buddha-fields within world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the western direction to hear the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, and the sound of the Saṅgha, and who wishes to establish those beings in right view, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to cause all those beings born in various Buddha-fields within world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the northern direction to hear the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, and the sound of the Saṅgha... [should train in the perfection of wisdom].
And one who wishes to establish those beings in right view should train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to cause all those beings born in various Buddha-fields throughout the world-systems in the northeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, to hear the sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," and the sound of "Saṅgha," and to establish those beings in right view, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Those who, desiring to establish all those beings born in various Buddha-fields throughout world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the southeastern direction— in the sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," and the sound of "Saṃgha"—
as well as those beings themselves in right view, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

Those who [desire to do so for] all those beings born in various Buddha-fields throughout world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the southwestern direction— in the sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," and the sound of "Saṃgha"...
One who wishes to establish those beings in right view should train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to cause all those beings born in various buddha-fields within the world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the northwestern direction to hear the sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," and the sound of "Saṃgha," and to establish them in right view, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to cause all those beings born in various Buddha-fields within world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the downward direction to hear the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, and the sound of the Saṅgha, and who wishes to establish those beings in right view, should train in the perfection of wisdom.

One who wishes to cause all those beings born in various Buddha-fields within world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the upward direction to hear the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, and the sound of the Saṅgha... [should train in the perfection of wisdom].
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to establish those beings in right view should train in the perfection of wisdom.
This is the analogy of the sound of joy accompanied by the summaries of the Dharma.
Moreover, Śāriputra, in the eastern direction, in worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā...

One should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "In all world-systems, in all buddha-fields, may those beings who are blind see forms with their eyes through my power; likewise, may those who are deaf hear sounds with their ears, and may those who are insane regain their mindfulness."
"Those who are naked shall obtain clothing;
those beings who are hungry shall have their bodies fulfilled;
and those who are thirsty shall be freed from thirst."
"May sentient beings born in the states of woe be liberated from all states of woe and obtain a human body;
I shall establish those of immoral conduct in the aggregate of ethical discipline."

"I shall establish those who are not concentrated in the aggregate of concentration; I shall establish those with poor wisdom in the aggregate of wisdom; I shall establish those who are not liberated in the aggregate of liberation."

"Thinking, 'I shall establish those who lack the knowledge and vision of liberation in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation,' or 'I shall establish those who have not yet seen the truths in the fruit of stream-entry,' or 'I shall establish them in the fruit of once-returning.'"
"I shall establish them in the fruit of non-returning," "I shall establish them in arhatship," "I shall establish them in pratyekabodhi."
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "I shall establish them in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "By my power, those beings who are blind in all the buddha-fields throughout the world-systems in the southern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, shall see forms with their eyes."
Thus, the deaf shall hear sounds with their ears;
the insane shall regain their mindfulness;
and the naked shall obtain clothing.
"May beings who are hungry have their bodies fully satisfied; may beings who are thirsty be freed from thirst;
and may beings born in the states of woe be liberated from all states of woe."
They will obtain a human existence;
I shall establish those of immoral conduct in the aggregate of ethical discipline; I shall establish those who are unconcentrated in the aggregate of meditative concentration.
"I shall establish those of poor wisdom in the aggregate of wisdom; I shall establish those who are unliberated in the aggregate of liberation;
I shall establish those lacking the knowledge and vision of liberation in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation."

"I shall establish those who have not yet seen the truths in the fruit of stream-entry; I shall establish them in the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and arhatship; I shall establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment."
"A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: 'I shall establish them in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

One should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: 'By my power, those beings who are blind in all Buddha-fields throughout the world-systems in the western direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, shall see forms with their eyes. Thus [should one train].
"The deaf shall hear sounds with their ears;
the insane shall regain their mindfulness;
and the naked shall obtain clothing."
"May beings who are hungry have their bodies fully satisfied; may beings who are thirsty be freed from thirst;
and may those beings born in the states of woe be liberated from all states of woe and obtain a human body."
"I shall establish those of immoral conduct in the aggregate of ethical discipline; I shall establish those who are unconcentrated in the aggregate of concentration;
I shall establish those of deficient wisdom in the aggregate of wisdom."

"Thinking, 'I shall establish those not yet liberated in the aggregate of liberation'; thinking, 'I shall establish those without the knowledge and vision of liberation in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation';
thinking, 'I shall establish those who have not seen the truths in the fruit of stream-entry'."

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "I shall establish [beings] in the fruit of once-returning, in the fruit of non-returning, and in arhatship; I shall establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; I shall establish them in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

One should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "May all beings who are blind in all the Buddha-fields throughout the world-systems in the northern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, behold forms with their eyes through my power. Likewise, one should train thinking: "May those who are deaf hear sounds with their ears."
"Those who are insane shall regain their mindfulness;
those who are naked shall obtain clothing;
and sentient beings who are hungry shall have their bodies fully nourished."
"May sentient beings who are thirsty become free from thirst;
may sentient beings born in the states of woe be liberated from all states of woe and obtain a human body;
and may I establish those of immoral conduct in the aggregate of ethical discipline."

"I shall establish those who are not concentrated in the aggregate of concentration; I shall establish those with poor wisdom in the aggregate of wisdom; I shall establish those who are not liberated in the aggregate of liberation."

"I shall establish those who lack the knowledge and vision of liberation in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation; I shall establish those who have not yet seen the truths in the fruit of stream-entry; I shall establish them in the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and in arhatship."
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "I shall establish them in pratyekabodhi; I shall establish them in unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening.
This applies to all sentient beings in all buddha-fields within world-systems as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River in the northeastern direction.
One should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "By my power, those who are blind shall see forms with their eyes";
likewise, "those who are deaf shall hear sounds with their ears," and "those who are insane shall regain their mindfulness."
"Those who are naked shall obtain clothes;
those beings who are hungry shall have their bodies fully satisfied;
and those beings who are thirsty shall be freed from thirst."
"May those beings born in the lower realms be liberated from all lower realms and obtain a human body; I shall establish those of immoral conduct in the aggregate of ethical discipline,
and I shall establish those who are unconcentrated in the aggregate of meditative concentration."
"I shall establish those of poor wisdom in the aggregate of wisdom; I shall establish those who are unliberated in the aggregate of liberation;
I shall establish those who lack the knowledge and vision of liberation in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation."

"I shall establish those who have not yet seen the truths in the fruit of stream-entry; I shall establish them in the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and arhatship; I shall establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment."
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "I shall establish them in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "By my power, those beings who are blind in all the buddha-fields throughout the world-systems in the southeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, shall see forms with their eyes."
Thus, the deaf shall hear sounds with their ears;
the insane shall regain their mindfulness;
and the naked shall obtain clothing.
"May beings who are hungry have their bodies fully satisfied; may beings who are thirsty be freed from thirst;
and may those beings born in the states of woe be liberated from all states of woe and obtain a human body."
"I shall establish those of immoral conduct in the aggregate of ethical discipline; I shall establish those who are unconcentrated in the aggregate of concentration;
I shall establish those of deficient wisdom in the aggregate of wisdom."

"I shall establish those who are not liberated in the aggregate of liberation; I shall establish those who lack the knowledge and vision of liberation in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation;
I shall establish those who have not seen the truths in the fruit of stream-entry."

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "I shall establish them in the fruit of once-returning, in the fruit of non-returning, and in arhatship; I shall establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; I shall establish them in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

One should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "May all beings who are blind in all the Buddha-fields throughout the world-systems in the south-western direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, see forms with their eyes through my power. Likewise, one should train thinking: "May those who are deaf hear sounds with their ears."
"Those who are insane shall regain their mindfulness;
those who are naked shall obtain clothing;
and hungry beings shall have their bodies fully nourished."
"May thirsty beings be freed from thirst;
may beings born in the states of woe be liberated from all states of woe and obtain a human body;
and may I establish those of immoral conduct in the aggregate of ethical discipline."

"I shall establish those who are not concentrated in the aggregate of concentration; I shall establish those with impaired wisdom in the aggregate of wisdom; I shall establish those who are not liberated in the aggregate of liberation."
"Thinking, 'I shall establish those who have not yet attained the knowledge and vision of liberation in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation';
'I shall establish those who have not yet seen the truths in the fruit of stream-entry';
'I shall establish them in the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and in arhatship.'"

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought, "I shall establish them in pratyekabodhi," and "I shall establish them in unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment.
This applies to all those in the buddha-fields within all the world-systems in the northwestern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.

One should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "May these blind beings, through my power, see forms with their eyes"; likewise, "may those who are deaf hear sounds with their ears," "may those who are insane regain their mindfulness," and "may those who are naked obtain clothing."
"May sentient beings who are hungry have their bodies fully satisfied; may sentient beings who are thirsty be freed from thirst;
and may sentient beings born in the states of woe be liberated from all states of woe and obtain a human body."
"I shall establish those of immoral conduct in the aggregate of ethical discipline; I shall establish those who are unconcentrated in the aggregate of concentration;
I shall establish those of deficient wisdom in the aggregate of wisdom."

"I shall establish those who are not liberated in the aggregate of liberation; I shall establish those who lack the knowledge and vision of liberation in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation;
I shall establish those who have not seen the truths in the fruit of stream-entry."

A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "I shall establish [beings] in the fruit of once-returning, in the fruit of non-returning, and in arhatship; I shall establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment; I shall establish them in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

One should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: "May all beings who are blind in all the Buddha-fields throughout the world systems in the downward direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, see forms with their eyes through my power; likewise, may those who are deaf hear sounds with their ears, and may those who are insane regain their mindfulness."
"Those who are naked shall obtain clothing;
those beings who are hungry shall have their bodies fully satisfied;
and those beings who are thirsty shall be freed from thirst."
"May those beings born in the states of woe be liberated from all states of woe and obtain a human body; I shall establish those of immoral conduct in the aggregate of ethical discipline,
and I shall establish those who are not concentrated in the aggregate of meditative concentration."
"I shall establish those of poor wisdom in the aggregate of wisdom; I shall establish those who are unliberated in the aggregate of liberation;
I shall establish those who lack the knowledge and vision of liberation in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation."

"I shall establish those who have not yet seen the truths in the fruit of stream-entry; I shall establish them in the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and arhatship; I shall establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment."
A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought, "I shall establish them in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

He should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought, "By my power, those beings who are blind in all the buddha-fields throughout the world-systems in the upward direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, shall see forms with their eyes. Thus [should he train].
"The deaf shall hear sounds with their ears;
the insane shall regain their mindfulness;
and the naked shall obtain clothing."
"May beings who are hungry have their bodies filled;
may beings who are thirsty be freed from thirst."
"May those beings reborn in the states of woe be liberated from all states of woe and obtain a human body; I shall establish the immoral in the aggregate of ethical discipline,
and I shall establish the unconcentrated in the aggregate of concentration."
"I shall establish those of poor wisdom in the aggregate of wisdom; I shall establish those who are unliberated in the aggregate of liberation;
I shall establish those who lack the knowledge and vision of liberation in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation."

"I shall establish those who have not yet seen the truths in the fruit of stream-entry; I shall establish them in the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and arhatship; I shall establish them in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment."
"A bodhisattva mahāsattva should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: 'I shall establish [beings] in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Thus, it is like the current of a river, accompanied by the path traveled by only one.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to train in the deportment of a Tathāgata should train in the perfection of wisdom."
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate in this way:
"When indeed shall I behold the elephant-look?
and "How may I walk with my feet without touching the earth by four finger-breadths? In this manner, he should train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate in this way:

"How might I [be surrounded] by the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśas, the Yāmas, the Tuṣitas, the Nirmāṇaratis, the Paranirmitavaśavartins, the Brahmakāyikas, the Brahmapurohitas, the Brahmapāriṣadyas, and the Parīttābhas?"

He was surrounded and escorted by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sons of gods from the Apramāṇābha, Ābhāsvara, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, Śubhakṛtsna, Anabhraka, Puṇyaprasava, Bṛhatphala, Asaṃjñisattva, Śuddhāvāsa, Avṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha heavens.
"One should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: 'May I approach the foot of the tree at the seat of awakening.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate in this way:
'How is it that the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa, the Yāma, the Tuṣita, the Nirmāṇarati, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin [heavenly realms]...'"

The Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, and Brahmapāriṣadya gods; the Parīttābha, Apramāṇābha, and Ābhāsvara gods; the Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, and Śubhakṛtsna gods; the Anabhraka, Puṇyaprasava, and Bṛhatphala gods; the Asaṃjñisattvas; and the Śuddhāvāsa gods—the Avṛha, Atapa, [Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha].
The Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha gods shall spread out a seat at the foot of the tree of enlightenment; thus should one train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate in this way:

"How may that spot of earth where I dwell—whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—become composed of diamond once I have awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment? In this way, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should train in the perfection of wisdom; furthermore, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, he should investigate in this manner.
"Why should I not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening on the very same day that I go forth? And on that very same day, why should I not turn the wheel of Dharma?
And while I am turning the wheel of Dharma, why should the Dharma-eye of incalculable and immeasurable beings—not free from dust and devoid of stain—not become purified regarding all phenomena?"

"One should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: 'May the minds of incalculable and immeasurable beings be liberated from all outflows through non-clinging; may incalculable and immeasurable beings become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate in this way:"
"How might my assembly of disciples be immeasurable and incalculable?
How might immeasurable and incalculable beings, through a single teaching of the Dharma, become bodhisattvas seated upon a single seat, non-retrogressive from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?
And how might there be an assembly of bodhisattvas that is both incalculable and immeasurable?"
"One should train in the perfection of wisdom with the thought: 'May my lifespan be immeasurable, and may my excellence of radiance be immeasurable.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate in this way:"

"How may it be that when I have awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, in that buddha-field the bases of passion, hatred, and delusion shall not exist at all, in every way, and in every respect?"—
thus should one train in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate in this way:

"How may sentient beings, when I have awakened to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, come to be endowed with such wisdom that the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, residing in other buddha-fields, might utter this inspired exclamation:
'Excellent is tranquility! Excellent is self-control! Excellent is restraint! Excellent is the practice of the holy life! Excellent is non-violence toward all living beings!'"
Thus should one train in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom should investigate in this way:
"How may it be that even after I have entered final nirvāṇa, there shall be no disappearance of the true Dharma?"

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom produces these qualities, such that upon merely hearing my name, the sentient beings in world-systems in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges become destined for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment— for this reason, one should train in the perfection of wisdom."
Then, those great kings who were in the triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system thought thus:

"We shall give four alms-bowls to this Bodhisattva, just as they were given by former great kings to former Tathāgatas. And the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāmas, the Tuṣitas, the Nirmāṇaratis, and the Paranirmitavaśavartins became joyful.
The gods will become eager, thinking,
"We shall perform services and attend upon this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva," and thus the hosts of Asuras will diminish while the divine hosts will increase.
And in the triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system, the Brahmapāriṣadyas, Brahmapurohitas, and Mahābrahmans became joyful;

the Parīttābhas, Apramāṇābhas, and Ābhāsvaras became joyful; as did the Parīttaśubhas, Apramāṇaśubhas, Śubhakṛtsnas, Anabhrakas, Puṇyaprasavas, Bṛhatphalas, Asaṃjñisattvas, Śuddhābhāsas, Avṛhas, and Atapas.
The Sudṛśas, the Sudarśanas, and the Akaniṣṭhas—these gods think thus:
"We shall entreat him, once he has attained perfect awakening, to turn the wheel of Dharma.
Śāriputra, at the time when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the perfection of wisdom, increases in the six perfections, [the gods think this].

At that time, the sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle become joyful, thinking, "We shall be his mother and father, his wife, children, kinsmen, and blood relations. The Four Great Kings, the gods of the Thirty-three, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods,
the Paranirmita-vaśavartin gods, the gods of Brahmā’s Retinue, and the gods of Brahmā’s Ministers likewise become joyful.
the gods of the Great Brahmās, the gods of Limited Purity, the gods of Immeasurable Purity, the gods of Radiant Splendor, the gods of Complete Purity,
the gods of Cloudless [Heaven], the gods of Merit-Born, the gods of Vast Fruit, the gods of Non-percipient Beings, the gods of the Pure Abodes, and the gods Free from Desire.
The Atapa gods, the Sudṛśa gods, the Sudarśana gods, and the Akaniṣṭha gods [surpass] the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva by virtue of his avoidance of sexual intercourse;
for from the first production of the thought of awakening onwards, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva remains a celibate practitioner of the holy life (*brahmacārī*).
He is not bound by the factors conducive to fetters;

it occurs to him: "For one who does not lead the holy life and who indulges in sensual pleasures, there will indeed be an obstacle even to rebirth in the Brahma-world, let alone to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."

"Therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva must awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment only after going forth from the home as one who practices celibacy, and not as one who does not practice celibacy.
When this had been said, the venerable Śāriputra addressed the Blessed One:
"But, Blessed One, must a bodhisattva necessarily have a mother and father, and must he necessarily have a wife, children, kinsmen, and blood relations?"
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Śāriputra:
"Śāriputra, for some bodhisattva mahāsattvas there are mothers and fathers, or wives, sons, kinsmen, and blood relations;

however, for other bodhisattva mahāsattvas, from the first production of the thought of awakening (prathamacittotpāda) onwards, having undertaken the holy life (brahmacarya), they practice the conduct of a bodhisattva while remaining in the state of a youth (kumārabhūta) [and attain] unsurpassed..."

Some awaken to unexcelled perfect enlightenment; some bodhisattva mahāsattvas, through skill in means, enjoy the five strands of sensual pleasure, go forth from the household life, and awaken to unexcelled perfect enlightenment.
Śāriputra, it is just as if, for example, there were a skilled illusionist or an apprentice of an illusionist who was well-trained in the art of illusion.
Having conjured up the five strands of sensual pleasure, he would delight in, play with, and enjoy those five strands of sensual pleasure.
What do you think, Śāriputra? Would those five strands of sensual pleasure have been tasted or enjoyed by that magician or the magician’s apprentice?
Śāriputra said:
"Certainly not, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
In the same way, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva enjoys the five strands of sensual pleasure through skill in means for the sake of maturing sentient beings;
yet the bodhisattva mahāsattva is not defiled by those sensual pleasures.
In this manner, the bodhisattva mahāsattva speaks in dispraise of sensual pleasures.
"Sensual pleasures are ablaze; sensual pleasures are loathsome; sensual pleasures are murderers; sensual pleasures are adversaries.
It is in this way, Śāriputra, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of maturing sentient beings, takes up the five strands of sensual pleasure.
Thus, accompanied by the desire for the Dharma, he is like a great cloud."
Thus has the production of the thought [of awakening] been described.
When this had been said, the venerable Śāriputra addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"Blessed One, how should a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom?"
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Śāriputra:
“In this regard, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom, while being a bodhisattva, does not perceive a bodhisattva,
nor does he perceive even the name ‘bodhisattva.’”
He does not perceive even the conduct of a bodhisattva, he does not perceive even the perfection of wisdom,
and he does not perceive even form.
In this way, he does not perceive feeling, perception, mental formations, or even consciousness.
Why is that?
Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva is empty of the intrinsic nature of a bodhisattva, and the perfection of wisdom is empty of the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
This is its very nature:
for form is not empty by means of emptiness,
nor is feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness empty by means of emptiness.
Emptiness is not other than form;
emptiness is not other than feeling;
emptiness is not other than perception.
Emptiness is not other than the formative forces;
emptiness is not other than consciousness. Why is that?
Form itself is emptiness.
Feeling itself is emptiness; perception itself is emptiness; mental formations themselves are emptiness.
Consciousness itself is emptiness;
emptiness itself is form;
emptiness itself is feeling.
Emptiness itself is perception; emptiness itself is mental formations;
emptiness itself is consciousness. For what reason?
For it is thus: that which is called "bodhisattva" is a mere name; that which is called "perfection of wisdom" is a mere name;
and that which is form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is a mere name.
For form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are like an illusion;
and an illusion is a mere name, neither located in a place nor in a region, non-existent and unproduced, equal to a false vision—
for such is the nature of the perception of an illusion.
There is neither arising nor cessation, neither affliction nor purification;
thus, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive even arising,
nor does he perceive even cessation.
He does not perceive affliction, nor does he perceive purification. Why is that?
Because for every phenomenon, "name" is merely a fabrication.
And those [dharmas] are conceptualized;
they are designated by adventitious names.
A bodhisattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom does not perceive any of these names; not perceiving them, he does not become attached to them.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not examine it in this way: "This which is called 'bodhisattva' is a mere name; this which is called 'awakening' (bodhi) is a mere name;
this which is called 'buddha' is a mere name."
This which is called "perfection of wisdom" is a mere name;
this which is called "practice in the perfection of wisdom" is a mere name;
this which is called "form" is a mere name.
This which is called "feeling" is a mere name; this which is called "perception" is a mere name; this which is called "volitional formations" is a mere name.
"This so-called 'consciousness' is a mere name;
for example, Śāriputra, it is called 'self,' yet no self is apprehended."
Neither a sentient being, nor a life-principle, nor a nourisher, nor a person, nor an individual, nor a human is apprehended, by virtue of the emptiness of non-apprehension. Why is that?
Because a bodhisattva does not even perceive that by which one might become attached.
Practicing in this way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva courses in the perfection of wisdom.
Śāriputra, suppose this Jambudvīpa were completely filled with monks like Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana,
just as a thicket of reeds, or a bamboo grove, or a field of sugarcane, or a thicket of *śara* grass, or a field of rice.
Or even the wisdom of all those sesame fields does not approach even a hundredth part of the wisdom of a bodhisattva practicing in the perfection of wisdom;
it does not approach a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor any number, nor a fraction, nor a calculation, nor a comparison, nor a likeness, nor even a resemblance.
In this way, Śāriputra, the wisdom cultivated by a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom for even a single day surpasses the wisdom of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
For it is so, Śāriputra, that the wisdom of a bodhisattva is present for the sake of the nirvāṇa of all sentient beings.
Let alone, Śāriputra, this Jambudvīpa filled with beings equal to you, Śāriputra, and Maudgalyāyana.
By monks. If, Śāriputra, this triple-thousand great-thousand world-system were filled with monks like Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana,
just as, for example, a thicket of reeds, or a bamboo grove, or a cane field, or a thicket of *śara* grass, or a field of rice.
Or even the wisdom of those [shravakas] compared to the wisdom cultivated by a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom for a single day does not approach even a hundredth part,
nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part; it does not admit of any number, fraction, calculation, or comparison.
It does not even approach a fraction, nor even a small part. Let alone, Śāriputra, a trichiliocosm world-system filled with monks like Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana.

If, Śāriputra, world-systems in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were filled with monks like Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, [it would still not approach a fraction of this merit].

It is just as if there were a grove of reeds, or a grove of bamboos, or a grove of sugarcane, or a grove of *śara* grass, or a grove of rice, or a grove of sesame; whatever wisdom those possess does not approach even a hundredth part, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor any numerical fraction of the wisdom cultivated by a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom for a single day.

It does not admit of even a fraction, nor a calculation, nor a comparison, nor a likeness, nor even a remote resemblance. Furthermore, Śāriputra, if world-systems in the southern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were filled with monks equal to Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana—
just as, for example, a thicket of reeds, or a grove of bamboos, or a forest of sugarcane, or a thicket of *śara* grass, or a field of rice.

Or even the wisdom of those [who have cultivated it] for an entire sesame field does not approach even a hundredth part of the wisdom of a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom who has cultivated it for a single day;
nor does it approach a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor any number, nor any fraction, nor any calculation, nor any comparison, nor any likeness, nor even a resemblance.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, if as many world systems in the western direction as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā were filled with monks equal to Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana— just as, for example, a thicket of reeds, a bamboo grove, a cane field, a forest of *śara* grass, a rice paddy, or a sesame field might be— the wisdom of all those [monks] would not approach even a hundredth part of the wisdom cultivated by a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom for a single day.

It does not approach even a thousandth part, nor even a hundred-thousandth part; it does not admit of any number, nor any fraction, nor any calculation, nor any comparison, nor any likeness, nor even a resemblance.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, if the world-systems in the northern direction were as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, and were filled with monks such as Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana—just as, for example, a thicket of reeds, or a forest of bamboos, or a grove of sugarcane, or a thicket of *śara* grass, or a field of rice, or a field of sesame seeds—[it would still not equal the merit of that person].
Or, whatever wisdom they possess does not approach even a hundredth part of the wisdom cultivated by a Bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom for a single day;
it does not approach a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor any number, nor a fraction, nor a calculation, nor a comparison, nor a likeness, nor even a resemblance.

If, Śāriputra, world-systems in the northeastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges were filled with monks equal to Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana— just as, for example, a thicket of reeds, a bamboo grove, a cane field, a thicket of grass, a field of rice, or a field of sesame seeds— the wisdom of all those monks would not equal the wisdom of a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom who has cultivated it for a single day.
It does not approach even a hundredth part of wisdom;
it does not approach a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor any number, nor a fraction, nor a calculation, nor a comparison, nor a likeness, nor even a remote resemblance.

Moreover, Śāriputra, if the world-systems in the southeastern direction were as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, and were filled with monks such as Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, [the merit of this would still surpass theirs].
It is just as if there were a grove of reeds, or a grove of bamboos, or a grove of sugarcane, or a grove of *śara* grass, or a grove of rice, or a grove of sesame;
whatever wisdom those possess does not approach even a hundredth part of the wisdom cultivated by a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom for a single day.
It does not approach even a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part; it does not admit of any number, fraction, calculation, comparison, likeness, or even a remote resemblance.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, if the world-systems in the southwestern direction were as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, and were filled with monks equal to Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, [the merit would still not approach that of the former].

It is just as if there were a forest of reeds, or a forest of bamboos, or a forest of sugarcane, or a forest of *śara* grass, or a forest of rice, or a forest of sesame; whatever wisdom those possess does not approach even a hundredth part, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor any numerical fraction of the wisdom cultivated by a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom for a single day.
It does not even admit of a fraction, a calculation, a comparison, a likeness, or a resemblance.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, if the world-systems in the northwestern direction were as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, and were filled with monks equal to Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana;
It is just as if there were a grove of reeds, or a grove of bamboos, or a grove of sugarcane, or a grove of *śara* grass, or a grove of rice, or a grove of sesame;
the wisdom possessed by all those [plants] does not approach even a hundredth part of the wisdom cultivated by a Bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom for a single day—
not even a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor any number, fraction, calculation, comparison, resemblance, or likeness.
If, Śāriputra, as many world-systems in the direction below as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā were filled with monks equal to Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana—

just as, for example, a thicket of reeds, or a bamboo grove, or a cane field, or a thicket of *śara* grass, or a field of rice, or a field of sesame— the wisdom of all those [monks] would not equal the wisdom of a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom who has cultivated it for a single day.
It does not approach even a hundredth part of wisdom;
it does not approach even a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor any number, nor a fraction, nor a calculation, nor a comparison, nor a likeness, nor even a subtle resemblance.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, if worlds in the upward direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā were filled with monks equal to Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, [it would still not approach even a hundredth part of wisdom].

It is just as if there were a grove of reeds, or a grove of bamboo, or a grove of sugarcane, or a grove of *śara* grass, or a grove of rice, or a grove of sesame; whatever wisdom those possess does not approach even a hundredth part of the wisdom cultivated by a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom for a single day—
it does not approach a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor any number, fraction, calculation, comparison, resemblance, or likeness.
Then the venerable Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One:

"Blessed One, that which is the wisdom of a stream-enterer, the wisdom of a once-returner, the wisdom of a non-returner, the wisdom of an arhat, the wisdom of a pratyekabuddha, the wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and the wisdom of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha— "
All these wisdoms are non-different, secluded, unarisen, without intrinsic nature, and empty.
And, Blessed One, no differentiation or distinction is perceived in that which is non-different, secluded, unarisen, without intrinsic nature, and empty.
How then, Blessed One, is the wisdom cultivated by a bodhisattva in a single day the wisdom of one practicing the perfection of wisdom compared to the wisdom of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Śāriputra:
"What do you think, Śāriputra? For what purpose is the cultivation for even a single day by a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom [superior]?"

Wisdom is present for one who courses in omniscience endowed with the excellence of all modes, acting for the benefit of all beings and perceiving all phenomena in all their aspects, thinking, "All sentient beings must be led to final nirvana.
Yet, Śāriputra, is wisdom present for all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas by virtue of that same task?
Śāriputra said:
"Certainly not, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:

What do you think, Śāriputra? Do all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ever think, "Having awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, we shall lead all sentient beings to final nirvana in the realm of nirvana without remainder"?
Śāriputra said:
"Certainly not, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:

Therefore, Śāriputra, by this method also you should understand it thus: whatever wisdom belongs to all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, that does not approach even a hundredth part, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor any number, fraction, or calculation of the wisdom of a bodhisattva cultivated for a single day.
It does not admit of being calculated, nor compared, nor approached by way of analogy, nor even by way of a mere fraction;
what do you think of that?
Śāriputra, do all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas ever think:

"Having practiced the six perfections, having matured sentient beings, having purified a buddha-field, and having fulfilled the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha..."
"Having fully realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, we shall lead immeasurable, incalculable, and infinite sentient beings to final nirvana.
Śāriputra said:
"Certainly not, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, it occurs to a bodhisattva mahāsattva thus:"

Having practiced the six perfections, having matured sentient beings, having purified the buddha-field, having fulfilled the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and having awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, [I shall deliver] immeasurable, incalculable, and infinite [beings].
"I shall lead sentient beings to final nirvāṇa"—
just as, Śāriputra, it does not occur to a firefly, a mere species of living creature, "By my light Jambudvīpa shall be illuminated," or "By my light Jambudvīpa shall be filled."

In the same way, Śāriputra, it does not occur to any of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas: "Having practiced even a single one of the six perfections, having matured sentient beings, having purified a buddha-field,
and having fulfilled the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities..."
"Having fulfilled the qualities of a Buddha and awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, I shall lead immeasurable, incalculable, and infinite sentient beings to final nirvāṇa.
Śāriputra, it is just as, for example, the orb of the sun, upon rising, illuminates the entire Jambudvīpa with its radiance.

In the same way, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having practiced the six perfections, having ripened sentient beings, having purified the buddha-field, having fulfilled the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, fully awakens to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"He brings immeasurable, incalculable, and infinite sentient beings to final nirvana.
When this had been said, the venerable Śāriputra addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"Blessed One, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having transcended the levels of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, reach the stage of non-retrogression and purify the path to awakening?"
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Śāriputra:

“In this regard, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, from the first production of the thought of awakening onwards, practicing the six perfections and abiding in all things as empty, signless, and wishless, attains the stage of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, the stage of non-retrogression, and purifies the path to awakening.”
When this had been said, the venerable Śāriputra addressed the Blessed One as follows:
“Blessed One, abiding on which stage does a bodhisattva mahāsattva become at all times and continuously worthy of offerings from all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?
When this had been said, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Śāriputra as follows:

Śāriputra, from the first production of the thought of awakening until he reaches the seat of enlightenment, while practicing the six perfections, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is at all times and continuously a worthy recipient of offerings for all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. Why is that?
For it is thus, Śāriputra: depending upon the bodhisattva mahāsattva, there occurs the manifestation in the world of all wholesome dharmas;

that is to say, the ten paths of wholesome action, the five precepts, the poṣadha endowed with eight limbs, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five... [superknowledges].

The manifestation in the world of the superknowledges, the four noble truths, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the noble eightfold path occurs.
The manifestation of the four grounds of self-confidence occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the four analytical knowledges occurs in the world;
and the manifestation of the six perfections, the ten powers of a Tathāgata, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha occurs in the world.
And through the manifestation of these wholesome qualities in the world, great kshatriya clans become known, great brahmin clans become known,
and great householder clans become known.
The gods of the Four Great Kings are known;
the gods of the Thirty-three are known;
the Yāma gods are known.
The Tuṣita gods are known;
the Nirmāṇarati gods are known; the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods are known.
The Brahmakāyika gods are known;
the Brahmapurohita gods are known;
the Mahābrahman gods are known.
The gods of Limited Radiance are known;
the gods of Immeasurable Radiance are known; the gods of Utmost Purity of Radiance are known.
The Parīttāśubha gods are known; the Apramāṇāśubha gods are known;
the Śubhakṛtsna gods are known.
The Anabhraka gods are known;
the Puṇyaprasava gods are known;
the Bṛhatphala gods are known.
The gods of the non-percipient beings are known;
the Śuddhāvāsa gods are known;
the Aspr̥ha gods are known.
The Atapa gods are known; the Sudṛśa gods are known;
the Sudarśana gods are known.
The Akaniṣṭha gods are known;
the Ākāśānantyāyatana gods are known;
the Vijñānānantyāyatana gods are known.
The gods of the sphere of nothingness are known; the gods of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception are known; and stream-enterers arise in the world.
Once-returners arise in the world,
non-returners arise in the world,
and arhats arise in the world.
Pratyekabuddhas arise in the world;
bodhisattvas arise in the world;
Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas arise in the world.
When this had been said, the venerable Śāriputra addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"But, Blessed One, does a bodhisattva mahāsattva purify the gift, or not?
The Blessed One replied:
For indeed, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not purify the gift;
why is that?
Because for a bodhisattva mahāsattva, the gift is already absolutely pure.
For what reason?
Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is a giver. Of what is he a giver?
He is a giver of wholesome dharmas. Of which wholesome dharmas is he a giver?
Namely: the ten paths of wholesome action, the five precepts, the poṣadha endowed with eight factors, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments,
the five superknowledges, the four noble truths, and the four foundations of mindfulness and the four right efforts.

He is the giver of the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, the noble eightfold path, the four grounds of self-confidence, the four analytical knowledges, the six perfections, the ten powers of a Tathāgata, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Thus ends the instruction on practice.
